long: CircleCI's MCP servers let coding agents diagnose build failures, inspect runs and manage CI pipelines through natural language without leaving the IDE. CircleCI offers a hosted MCP server at mcp.circleci.com and a CircleCI CLI MCP that runs locally with your CLI credentials.

The older local npm package (@circleci/mcp-server-circleci) is deprecated in favor of the hosted server and CLI MCP. Hosted tools cover listing runs, workflows and jobs, reading logs and tests, and rerunning or canceling workflows. The CLI MCP exposes the wider CircleCI CLI, including config authoring and orb tooling. Cloud plans listed on the docs page include Free, Performance and Scale.
circleci-mcp.who: Developers who use CircleCI and want an AI coding assistant to investigate failed builds, read logs and act on workflows from the editor.
features: Hosted MCP server and CircleCI CLI MCP
Inspect runs, workflows, jobs, logs and tests
Rerun or cancel workflows from the assistant
Natural-language CI diagnostics in the IDE
faq: What happened to the old CircleCI MCP npm package?
CircleCI deprecated the local @circleci/mcp-server-circleci package and points users to the hosted MCP server and the CircleCI CLI MCP instead.
Hosted server or CLI MCP?
Use the hosted server for day-to-day diagnostics (failures, logs, reruns). Use the CLI MCP when you also need config authoring, orbs or other admin CLI tasks.
Which CircleCI plans support it?
The overview docs list Cloud plans Free, Performance and Scale.

long: Roo Code is discontinued. Its official README says the Roo Code extension was shut down on May 15, 2026, and the repository is archived. It remains under the Apache 2.0 license, so the code can still be read and forked.

Before the shutdown, Roo Code was an open-source AI coding agent for VS Code. It could generate code from natural-language specs, refactor and debug existing code, write documentation, answer questions about a codebase and use MCP servers, with Code, Architect, Ask, Debug and custom modes. The README points users to Cline, the project Roo Code was forked from, and to ZooCode, a community fork.
roo-code.who: Existing Roo Code users planning a migration, and developers studying its mode-based agent design. New users should start with an actively maintained alternative.
features: Discontinued: the extension shut down on May 15, 2026, and the repo is archived
Was a VS Code coding agent with Code, Architect, Ask, Debug and custom modes
Apache 2.0 code you can still fork
Suggested alternatives: Cline and the community fork ZooCode
faq: Is Roo Code still available?
No. The Roo Code extension was shut down on May 15, 2026, according to its official README, and the repository is archived. Billing questions go to billing@roocode.com.

long: Devin is Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer. It runs in the cloud or on your machine, tests its work in its own browser and keeps going until a pull request is ready to merge. You can start it from Devin Cloud, from Devin Desktop or the CLI, or by tagging @Devin in Slack or Teams.

Beyond writing code, it can run automations that react to bugs, failed CI and alerts. Devin Wiki maps a codebase and its architecture, and Devin Review checks pull requests for bugs and vulnerabilities. On the official pricing page, the Free plan comes with a light quota. Pro costs $20 a month and adds Devin Cloud, Max costs $200 a month, and Teams costs $80 a month plus $40 for each full developer seat. Enterprise plans add SAML/OIDC SSO and a VPC deployment option.
devin.who: Engineering teams that want to hand off tickets, bug fixes, migrations and reviews to an agent that opens pull requests, while keeping humans in the review loop.
features: Runs in the cloud (Devin Cloud) or locally (Devin Desktop and CLI)
Tests changes in its own browser before opening a PR
Tag @Devin in Slack and Teams; Linear and Jira integrations
Automations for bugs, failed CI and alerts
Devin Wiki codebase maps and Devin Review PR checks
Free plan; Pro $20/mo, Max $200/mo, Teams $80/mo plus $40 per seat
faq: How much does Devin cost?

According to Cognition's pricing page: a Free plan with a light quota, Pro at $20/month (which adds Devin Cloud), Max at $200/month, Teams at $80/month plus $40/month per full dev seat, and custom Enterprise plans.

tiers: light agent quota, unlimited inline edits and Tab completions
higher quotas, frontier models from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and SpaceXAI
plus $40/mo per full dev seat, up to 200 users
pricing_v.note: Extra usage on paid plans is billed at API pricing.

long: Windsurf has been rebranded as Devin Desktop. Cognition's official page says: "Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf." Devin Desktop keeps Windsurf's full IDE and adds an Agent Command Center, with Spaces, a Kanban view and multi-agent management, for running local and cloud agents from one place.

Existing Windsurf users get Devin Desktop as an over-the-air update, and their plan, pricing, extensions and settings carry over. Cognition says Windsurf for JetBrains IDEs is still available to download. Devin Desktop works with other agents through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) and includes Supercomplete, Fast Context and the SWE-2 model. Plans are Free, Pro at $20 a month, Max at $200 a month, and Teams.
windsurf.who: Windsurf users following the product into Devin Desktop, and developers who want one AI IDE to manage several local and cloud coding agents.
features: Rebranded: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (Cognition)
Agent Command Center: Spaces, Kanban view, multi-agent management
Full IDE with Supercomplete and Fast Context
Agent Client Protocol (ACP) support for other agents
Hand off a plan to the cloud with Devin Cloud
Windsurf for JetBrains is still available
faq: What happened to Windsurf?
Cognition renamed it Devin Desktop. Existing users get it as an over-the-air update, and their plan, pricing, extensions and settings carry over, including legacy Windsurf Enterprise plans.
How much does Devin Desktop cost?
The official page lists Free, Pro at $20/month, Max at $200/month, and Teams plans.

facts.status: Rebranded as Devin Desktop by Cognition; windsurf.com/pricing redirects to Devin's pricing

pricing_v.note: windsurf.com/pricing now redirects to Devin's pricing page: Windsurf has been rebranded as Devin Desktop, and these are Devin's plans.

long: AutoGen is Microsoft's open-source framework for building multi-agent AI applications that can act on their own or alongside people. Its official README now says the project has been archived and is no longer actively maintained. Microsoft no longer provides bug fixes, security fixes, new features or support, and it advises against production use.

Microsoft recommends that new users start with Microsoft Agent Framework, which it calls AutoGen's enterprise-ready successor, and it publishes a migration guide for existing users. AutoGen needs Python 3.10 or later. It ships AgentChat and Core APIs, extensions for model clients and tools such as MCP, and AutoGen Studio, a no-code GUI for prototyping multi-agent workflows.
autogen.who: Researchers and teams maintaining existing AutoGen projects or studying multi-agent patterns. New production work should use Microsoft Agent Framework.
features: Archived: no longer maintained by Microsoft (per the README)
Successor: Microsoft Agent Framework, with a migration guide
AgentChat and Core APIs for multi-agent apps (Python 3.10+)
Extensions for model clients and MCP tools
faq: Is AutoGen still maintained?
No. The official README says AutoGen has been archived and is no longer actively maintained by Microsoft. New users should start with Microsoft Agent Framework.

facts.license: MIT for code (LICENSE-CODE); CC-BY-4.0 for documentation
facts.status: Microsoft's official README says AutoGen is archived and no longer actively maintained

long: Comet is Perplexity's AI browser. It's built on Chromium, uses Perplexity search as its main search engine, and has a built-in assistant that can understand pages, create content and take on tasks for you. Comet is available for Mac, Windows, iOS and Android.

According to Perplexity's help center, its main features are Personal Search, which uses your browsing history; natural-language browser commands for managing tabs; a Gmail connector for email and calendar questions; Ask and Summarize buttons for the page you're on; and built-in ad blocking. It also has standard browser features and supports most Chrome extensions.
comet.who: People who want an everyday browser with an AI assistant that can answer questions about pages, summarize them and take on web tasks.
features: Perplexity AI search as the default engine
Comet Assistant for page questions and delegated tasks
Gmail connector, Ask and Summarize buttons, built-in AdBlock

long: The NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform is a reference architecture for monitoring AI agents continuously, which NVIDIA announced on its technical blog on September 28, 2026. It combines NVIDIA OpenShell, an open-source secure runtime that runs autonomous agents in sandboxes with kernel-level isolation, with NVIDIA Sentry running on BlueField-4 DPUs.

Sentry uses NVIDIA DOCA to extend monitoring and enforcement into the hardware. It links agent interactions, policy decisions and tool access into records of agent activity. In Vera Rubin POD systems, the DPU sits on the node's only path to the model, which gives out-of-band visibility and real-time policy enforcement. NVIDIA describes five principles: verifiable policy, out-of-band enforcement, controlling the path to the model, scaling agent authority with how visible its reasoning is, and shared responsibility.
nvidia-open-agent-safety-platform.who: Platform and security teams designing how autonomous agents are contained and monitored, especially on NVIDIA infrastructure. OpenShell can be used on its own.
features: OpenShell: open-source sandboxed agent runtime with kernel-level isolation
NVIDIA Sentry on BlueField-4 DPUs for out-of-band monitoring
Correlates agent interactions, policy decisions and tool access
Hardware layer targets NVIDIA Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin POD systems

long: CoreWeave Forge is a platform for building and improving models and agents, launched on September 30, 2026. It covers the whole loop of running, observing, curating, improving and evaluating in one connected environment. It combines Weights & Biases Models, OpenPipe's post-training expertise and marimo-based notebooks with CoreWeave's own services, and it works with other models, frameworks and clouds.

At launch it included ARIA, a coding agent that analyzes experiment and agent-observability data and proposes next steps. It also included Agent Lens for observing production agents, Sandboxes for isolated runs, Registry for versioned checkpoints and agent configs, Post-Training (serverless RL and fine-tuning) and Inference. The Free plan costs $0 a month. Pro starts at $60 a month with a 30-day trial and is meant for teams with fewer than 50 employees. Enterprise is custom.
coreweave-forge.who: ML and agent teams that want tracing, evals, sandboxes and post-training in one place, including existing Weights & Biases users.
features: Agent Lens observability for production agents
Sandboxes for agent tool use, RL and evals
ARIA agent that proposes next experiments
faq: How much does CoreWeave Forge cost?
Free is $0/month. Pro starts at $60/month (billed monthly, 30-day free trial) for teams with fewer than 50 employees. Enterprise is custom-priced.

long: Autoloop is the agent optimization engine in Kore.ai's Artemis agent platform, released on October 13, 2026. Teams set the goals an agent should meet. Autoloop then evaluates the agent against those goals, traces failures to their root cause, applies targeted fixes and re-checks every change for regressions before keeping it.

Goals cover seven dimensions: task completion, accuracy and grounding, business-rule adherence, token and cost efficiency, end-user experience, robustness, and guardrails and safety. Problems that can be fixed deterministically, such as contracts, fixtures and routing rules, are repaired directly, and models are used where judgment is needed. Changes can be applied in three modes: Autopilot applies them automatically, Copilot waits for a person to approve, and Advisor only recommends them.
kore-ai-autoloop.who: Enterprises running complex networks of production agents on Kore.ai that need agent quality to improve continuously without regressions.
features: Traces failures across multi-agent paths to root cause
Every change gated and re-verified against all goals

long: nanoMuse is an open-source personal agent for all your devices. It's a single agent with its own name and look that takes actions instead of just answering questions, keeps working while the app is closed, remembers you and asks before doing anything you couldn't undo. The phone app, desktop app, web console and the relay that connects them are all in one repository, licensed GPL-3.0-or-later.

It can use a Linux shell, a browser, MCP servers and skills. With Hands turned on, it can operate apps on your phone and windows on your computer through the screen. Signing in gives you a free allowance of model use on the community relay. After that you can use your own API key or run the relay on your own server. Version 1.0.0 came out on October 9, 2026, and builds are available for Android, iPhone (TestFlight beta), macOS, Windows, Linux and Docker.
nanomuse.who: Tinkerers and developers who want a self-hostable personal agent across phone and desktop, with their own model key and approvals before risky actions.
features: Phone, desktop and web apps plus a self-hostable relay
Shell, browser, MCP servers and skills; screen control with Hands
Asks before deleting, sending or paying
Routines and goals that run while the app is closed
Free community-relay allowance, then bring your own key

long: Flowise is discontinued. The team announced on July 29, 2026 that it was winding the project down and froze the code. The GitHub repository was archived on August 13, 2026, and npm packages and Docker images were marked deprecated. End of life was August 31, 2026, when the core team stopped taking part on Discord and GitHub.

Flowise was an open-source platform for building agents visually. It offered Agentflow for multi-agent systems, Chatflow for single-agent chatbots with tool calling and RAG, human-in-the-loop review, and execution traces. The Apache 2.0 code stays on GitHub, and the team encourages people to fork it.
flowise.who: Teams with existing Flowise deployments planning a migration or maintaining a fork. New projects should pick an actively maintained builder.
features: Discontinued: end of life Aug 31, 2026 (repo archived Aug 13, 2026)
Was a visual builder: Agentflow (multi-agent) and Chatflow (chat assistants)
Tool calling, RAG, human-in-the-loop, execution traces
Apache 2.0 code remains available to fork
faq: Is Flowise still maintained?
No. Flowise reached end of life on August 31, 2026. The repository was archived on August 13, 2026, and the team encourages forking the Apache 2.0 code.

long: Replit Agent turns plain-language ideas into apps, designs, slides and more, and you don't need to know how to code. Unlike a chatbot, it takes action: it sets up the project, writes code, sets up infrastructure, tests the result and fixes problems along the way, from planning through deployment.

Plan mode lets you work out an ordered task list before any code changes. Agent modes control cost and capability. Free Mode covers everyday work within your plan's allowance, and the paid Power and Max modes use stronger models. One project can include web apps, mobile apps, data dashboards, slides and videos that share a backend. It can also pull data from connected services such as BigQuery, Linear, Slack and Notion.
replit-agent.who: Founders, makers and non-developers who want to build and publish working apps from a prompt in the browser, and developers who want fast prototypes.
features: Builds, tests and publishes apps from plain language
Plan mode for ordered task lists before building
Free, Power and Max agent modes
Web apps, mobile apps, slides, dashboards and videos in one project
Connectors for BigQuery, Linear, Slack, Notion and more
faq: Do I need to know how to code to use Replit Agent?
No. Replit's docs say Agent handles the technical work from planning to deployment.

long: MyShell describes itself as an AI consumer layer where people can build, share and own AI agents. It has its own $SHELL token. The site is currently built around MyShell Art, launched on June 4, 2026, which creates portraits, filters and short videos from a selfie.

MyShell Art is powered by Shell Agent and offers 200+ styles across professional, artistic, fashion and trending categories. Examples include headshot generators, storyboard and one-image film generators, cartoon and pixel-art styles, and virtual try-ons. MyShell says you can start creating for free.
myshell.who: Casual creators who want quick AI portraits, filters and short videos, and builders interested in MyShell's agent and token ecosystem.
features: Build, share and own AI agents
MyShell Art: 200+ portrait, filter and video styles

long: Almanax is an AI security engineer for application security. It connects to your GitHub repositories, scans for vulnerabilities and reviews every pull request so it can block risky code before merging. It has specialized models for blockchain ecosystems such as EVM, Solana, Stellar and Aptos, and it also supports most programming languages.

Its features include automated threat modeling, custom detection rules written in plain English, agents that learn from dismissed findings, reachability triage of third-party alerts and automatic patch suggestions. In June 2026, Almanax announced that it was joining the product-security company depthfirst, which acquired it. The Almanax site is still live and offers a 7-day free trial.
almanax.who: Security and engineering teams, especially at blockchain and smart-contract companies, that want continuous AI code scanning and PR review instead of only periodic audits.
features: GitHub app for repo scans and PR security reviews
Automated threat modeling and custom natural-language rules
Third-party alert triage with reachability analysis
faq: Is Almanax still independent?
No. In June 2026 Almanax announced that it was joining depthfirst, which acquired the company. The Almanax site is still live and offers a 7-day free trial.

long: Laika AI's site now presents Polymetric by Laika AI, an analytics and intelligence platform built on Polymarket's public on-chain data. The site describes it as a Bloomberg Terminal for prediction markets. Earlier, it was listed as a Web3 browser extension for crypto research.

Polymetric offers AI-generated research on open prediction markets, whale-wallet tracking, a market screener and a live news feed. It covers more than 18,000 active Polymarket markets across politics, crypto, economics, entertainment and sports. It only reads public on-chain data, never asks your wallet to sign anything and doesn't handle user funds.
laika-ai.who: Polymarket traders who want AI research, whale tracking and screening on top of public prediction-market data.
features: Polymarket screener by volume, liquidity and edge
Read-only: never asks your wallet to sign

long: Sharpe Terminal, from Sharpe Labs Ltd. (founded 2021), is a free crypto derivatives, DEX and market-intelligence terminal. It combines funding rates, futures data, arbitrage scanners, listings, narratives, memecoins, news and research in more than 20 trader tools, and core analytics need no signup.

For AI agents, Sharpe offers an MCP server that brings live market data into Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT and other agents. It's hosted at sharpe.ai/api/mcp or can run locally with npx. Sharpe also offers a REST API with an OpenAPI spec and a CLI with JSON and CSV output. Its data covers funding rates across 42 exchanges and futures across 10.
sharpe-labs.who: Crypto traders and quant-minded builders who want free derivatives and market data, and agent builders who want that data available through MCP.
features: Free web terminal, no signup for core analytics
Funding rates across 42 exchanges; futures, OI, liquidations, arbitrage
Rug Check, new listings, narratives and memecoin trackers
MCP server (hosted or npx) for Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT

tiers: or $1,490 a year; 500,000 requests a month
pricing_v.note: Every chart on Sharpe Terminal is free with no signup. The REST API, MCP server and CLI share one key.

long: Pi is a minimal, extensible agent harness from Earendil that you can run as an interactive terminal coding agent, in print/JSON mode for scripts, as an RPC server over stdin/stdout, or as a TypeScript SDK embedded in your own app. Pi 1.0 shipped together with Pi Durable, a durable conversation, task and document runtime.

It deliberately leaves out built-in sub-agents and plan mode: you add what you need with TypeScript extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes, bundled as Pi packages and shared over npm or git. It works with 15+ providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock, Mistral, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter, Ollama and more), can switch models mid-session, and stores sessions as branchable trees you can export to HTML or share as a gist.
pi.who: Developers who want a small, hackable terminal coding agent they can reshape with their own extensions, and teams that want to embed an agent loop in their own product (the project cites OpenClaw as a real-world integration).
features: Interactive TUI, print/JSON, RPC and SDK modes
Extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes as npm or git packages
Tree-structured sessions with HTML export and gist sharing
AGENTS.md / SYSTEM.md context control and customizable compaction
faq: Does Pi sandbox the commands it runs?
No. Pi has no built-in permission system and runs with the permissions of the user who starts it; its docs recommend running it in a container or sandbox if you need stronger boundaries.
How do I install Pi?
Use the installer from pi.dev (curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh, or the PowerShell script on Windows) or npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. It needs Node.js 22.19 or newer.

long: CLI-Anything, from the HKUDS lab, turns existing software, codebases and web APIs into agent-native command-line interfaces, so AI agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, nanobot and Pi can operate that software without a GUI.

Generated CLIs are published to CLI-Hub, a community registry you use with pip install cli-anything-hub and cli-hub install <name>, or hand to an agent as a skill. The project's demos show agents driving FreeCAD, Blender and draw.io through generated CLIs to finished CAD models, 3D scenes and diagrams, and a technical report is on arXiv.
cli-anything.who: Agent builders whose agents need to control desktop or specialist software (CAD, 3D, diagramming, media tools) that has no agent-friendly API, and contributors who want to publish CLIs for others to reuse.
features: Generates agent-ready CLIs for existing software and web APIs
Installable as an agent skill for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and others
Demos for FreeCAD, Blender and draw.io
faq: How do agents use CLI-Anything?
Install the CLI-Hub skill or the cli-anything-hub Python package, then ask the agent to find a matching CLI in CLI-Hub and complete the task with it.

long: skills is Vercel Labs' open-source command-line tool for the open agent skills ecosystem: npx skills add owner/repo installs reusable skills (instructions plus supporting files) into coding agents such as OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 75 more.

It can pull skills from GitHub, GitLab, Azure Repos, any git URL or a local folder, install them globally or per project, and npx skills use generates a prompt for a single skill without installing it. The companion site skills.sh is a directory of skills with an install leaderboard.
skills-sh.who: Developers who use one or more coding agents and want to install, share and update the same skills across all of them, including from private repositories.
features: npx skills add and npx skills use
Supports OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 75+ other agents
Sources: GitHub, GitLab, Azure Repos, any git URL or a local path
Private repos via your existing git, GitHub CLI or SSH authentication
skills.sh directory with an install leaderboard
faq: Does skills need my GitHub token?
Not normally. It uses the git, GitHub CLI or SSH authentication you already have; GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN can be set explicitly for API access to private repositories.

long: MarkItDown is Microsoft's lightweight Python utility for converting files to Markdown for use with LLMs and text-analysis pipelines. It keeps important document structure, such as headings, lists, tables and links, as Markdown.

It converts PDF, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, images (EXIF metadata and OCR), audio (metadata and speech transcription), HTML, CSV, JSON and XML, ZIP files, YouTube URLs and EPubs. The output is meant for machines to read rather than for high-fidelity documents for people.
markitdown.who: Developers building LLM, RAG or agent pipelines who need to turn Office files, PDFs and other documents into clean Markdown before sending them to a model.
features: Converts PDF, Word, PowerPoint and Excel files to Markdown
Keeps headings, lists, tables and links
OCR and EXIF metadata for images; transcription for audio
Handles HTML, CSV, JSON, XML, ZIP archives, EPubs and YouTube URLs
faq: Is MarkItDown safe to run on untrusted files?
Its README warns that MarkItDown performs I/O with the privileges of the current process, so you should sanitize inputs in untrusted environments and call the narrowest convert function you need.

long: Ollama lets you run open models locally on macOS, Windows and Linux, or in the cloud, and gives you a CLI and a REST API for running and managing them. An official Docker image and Python and JavaScript libraries are available.

It can connect models to coding agents and apps such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and OpenCode, and to OpenClaw for a personal assistant across chat apps. Its local backend is built on the llama.cpp project.
ollama.who: Developers and hobbyists who want to run open-weight models on their own machine and plug them into agents, chat interfaces or their own apps through a local API.
features: Run open models locally on macOS, Windows and Linux
REST API plus official Python and JavaScript libraries
One-command launch of integrations such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
Model library at ollama.com/library and Modelfile customization

long: Open WebUI is a self-hosted AI platform built to run entirely offline. It works with Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API, so you can use local and cloud models from one provider-agnostic interface.

It installs with pip, uv, Docker or Kubernetes and adds role-based access control and user groups for teams. Plugins (filters, actions, pipes, tools and skills) and MCP, MCPO and OpenAPI tool servers extend it. An enterprise plan is offered by its maker.
open-webui.who: Individuals and teams who want a private, self-hosted ChatGPT-style interface for local models (via Ollama) and cloud APIs, with user management and plugins.
features: Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API (LM Studio, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, vLLM and more)
Role-based access control and user groups
Plugins: filters, actions, pipes, tools and skills
MCP, MCPO and OpenAPI tool servers
Install via pip, uv, Docker or Kubernetes

long: CC Switch is a desktop app (built with Tauri) for managing coding-agent CLIs from one place: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi and others.
It switches API providers in one click and manages MCP servers, skills and prompts, so you don't have to hand-edit JSON, TOML or YAML config files. Its only official website is ccswitch.io.
cc-switch.who: Developers who use several AI coding CLIs or API providers and want to switch between them and manage MCP servers and skills without editing config files.
features: Manages MCP servers, skills and prompts in one place
Supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenClaw and more
No hand-editing of JSON, TOML or YAML configs

long: Zed is a high-performance, multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter. You can download it for macOS, Linux and Windows or install it through a package manager.
Its source code is licensed primarily under GPL-3.0-or-later, with Apache-2.0 components where marked. A web version is not yet available.
zed.who: Developers who want a fast, native code editor with real-time collaboration and built-in AI features, and who prefer an open-source editor.
features: High-performance native editor written in Rust
Available for macOS, Linux and Windows

long: Scrapling is a Python web-scraping framework that combines fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, parsing and concurrent crawling in one library. It can scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with sites and capture the API calls behind them.

Crawlers get reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause and resume, and exports to JSON, JSONL, CSV and XML. You can use it from Python, the terminal, or an AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill.
scrapling.who: Developers and data teams who need to scrape or crawl websites, including JavaScript-heavy ones, and AI-agent builders who want a scraping MCP server.
features: Fast HTTP fetching plus stealth browsers and JavaScript rendering
CSS, XPath, text and regex selection with adaptive element tracking
Concurrent spiders with proxy rotation, retries and pause/resume
Exports to JSON, JSONL, CSV and XML, or clean Markdown
MCP server, Agent Skill, CLI and interactive shell

long: LobeHub (formerly Lobe Chat) is an open-source workspace for running AI agents. Its README describes it as organizing your agents into round-the-clock operation: it hires, schedules and reports on your AI team while you stay in charge.
It can be deployed with Docker or on Vercel, and has an official site, documentation and changelog.
lobehub.who: Individuals and teams who want a self-hostable, open-source interface to create, run and coordinate many AI agents.
features: Create and manage multiple AI agents
Schedules agents and reports on their work
Self-host with Docker or deploy on Vercel

long: OmniRoute is a free, open-source AI gateway that routes requests across many model providers. You bring your own provider accounts and it catalogs and pools their free tiers, showing what is available on a dashboard.
Its README stresses that the token totals it shows are an estimate across third-party free tiers, not a grant from OmniRoute; each provider controls its own limits, availability and terms.
omniroute.who: Developers who want one gateway in front of many LLM providers, especially to combine free tiers they already have accounts for.
features: Single gateway across many LLM providers
Bring your own provider accounts and keys
Catalog of provider free tiers with a live dashboard

long: Headroom compresses what your AI agent reads (tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, files and conversation history) before it reaches the LLM, to cut token usage. Compression runs on your own machine.

You can use it as a Python or TypeScript library, as a local proxy with no code changes, as a wrapper around coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Aider, or as an MCP server. Originals are cached locally so compressed content can be retrieved.
headroom.who: Developers running coding agents or LLM apps who want to reduce token costs and context usage without changing their models.
features: Local proxy mode with no code changes
Wraps Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, OpenCode, Cline and more
MCP server with compress, retrieve and stats tools
Runs locally; originals cached for retrieval

long: HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Its tagline is "Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents."

You can use it locally through its CLI, from AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode through plugins and skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows.
hyperframes.who: Developers and AI-agent users who want to generate videos from code or prompts, such as product intros, with repeatable output.
features: Renders HTML, CSS, media and animations to MP4
Plugins and skills for Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode

long: Warp is an agentic development environment that grew out of the terminal. You can use its built-in coding agent or bring your own CLI agent, such as Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI.

Its client codebase is open source: the UI framework crates are MIT-licensed and the rest of the repository is AGPL v3. Warp also offers Warp Factories, infrastructure for teams to run cloud software factories of agents.
warp.who: Developers who live in the terminal and want a modern terminal with a built-in coding agent, or a home for the CLI agents they already use.
features: Modern terminal with a built-in coding agent
Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and other CLI agents
Warp Drive for shared workflows and docs
Warp Factories for teams running agents in the cloud
Open-source client (AGPL v3, MIT UI framework)

long: PPT Master is an open-source project that uses AI to generate native, editable PowerPoint files from source documents such as PDFs, DOCX files and web pages.
It identifies key points, structures the narrative and produces a PPTX you can keep refining in PowerPoint. The project is released under the MIT License and is kept free with the help of sponsors.
ppt-master.who: People who regularly turn reports and documents into slide decks and want an open-source, AI-driven way to get editable PowerPoint files.
features: Works from PDFs, Word documents and web pages
Extracts key points and structures the narrative

long: LiteLLM is an open-source AI gateway that gives you one interface to call 100+ LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock and Azure, using the OpenAI format.

You can use it as a Python SDK inside your code or deploy the AI Gateway (proxy server) as a central service for a team, with virtual keys, spend tracking, guardrails, load balancing and an admin dashboard. A hosted proxy and an enterprise tier are also offered.
litellm.who: Developers and platform teams who call several LLM providers and want one OpenAI-compatible API, plus central keys, budgets and spend tracking.
features: One OpenAI-format API for 100+ LLM providers
Python SDK and self-hosted AI Gateway (proxy server)
Virtual keys, spend tracking and budgets
Endpoints for chat, responses, embeddings, images, audio, batches and rerank

long: MemPalace is a local-first memory system for AI agents. It stores your conversation history as verbatim text and retrieves it with semantic search, without summarizing or paraphrasing it.

Its index is structured so searches can be scoped (people and projects become wings, topics become rooms), and the retrieval backend is pluggable, with ChromaDB as the default. Nothing leaves your machine unless you opt in. Its README warns that the only official sources are the GitHub repo, the PyPI package and mempalaceofficial.com.
mempalace.who: Developers using coding agents such as Claude Code who want long-term, local memory of past sessions that they can search.
features: Verbatim storage of conversation history (no summarizing)
Semantic search scoped by wings and rooms
Local-first: nothing leaves your machine unless you opt in

long: PrivateGPT is an open-source API layer that turns local models into AI applications. It follows the Claude API model and provides the backend building blocks (messages, ingestion, retrieval and tools) so you can build private AI products without depending on cloud APIs.
It does not run models itself: it connects to any OpenAI-compatible inference server. It ships a workbench UI at /ui for testing, and it powers Zylon, an on-premise AI platform for enterprises.
privategpt.who: Developers and companies building private or on-premise AI apps on local models who need RAG, tools and ingestion without rebuilding a backend.
features: Messages API with streaming, async and token counting
Retrieval with citations and agentic RAG
Built-in tools (web search, web fetch, code execution), custom tools and MCP connectors
Structured access to databases and CSVs
Works with any OpenAI-compatible inference server

long: Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI. It began as Alibaba Group's internal AI code review assistant and was later released as open source.

It reads Git diffs and sends changed files to a configurable LLM through an agent that can read full files and search the codebase, then writes structured review comments with line-level precision. An ocr scan command reviews whole files for audits.
open-code-review.who: Engineering teams that want automated, line-level AI code reviews on their own model endpoint, run from the command line or CI.
features: Reviews Git diffs with line-level comments
Agent can read files, search the codebase and inspect related changes
Works with a configurable model endpoint
Originated as Alibaba's internal review assistant

long: LibreChat is an open-source, self-hosted chat interface that works with many AI providers, often described as an enhanced ChatGPT clone with multi-provider support.

Recent releases (v0.8.8) add an Agent Management API in beta, experimental attached workspaces where agents can read files and run commands, and admin controls to ask, allow or deny file writes and command execution.
librechat.who: Teams and individuals who want to self-host one chat app for several AI providers, with agents and admin controls.
features: Self-hosted chat for multiple AI providers
Agents with files and skills, plus an Agent Management API (beta)
Code approval controls: ask, allow or deny writes and commands
Context usage and manual context compaction

long: Jan is an open-source ChatGPT replacement for your desktop. You can download and run LLMs such as Llama, Gemma, Qwen and gpt-oss from Hugging Face with full control and privacy, or connect to cloud models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq and others.
It runs a local OpenAI-compatible API server at localhost:1337 for other apps, supports MCP for agentic features, and is available for Windows, macOS and Linux.
jan.who: People who want a private, desktop AI chat app that runs models locally, and developers who need a local OpenAI-compatible API.
features: Download and run local LLMs from Hugging Face
Connect cloud models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq and more

long: Kong Gateway is a cloud-native, platform-agnostic API, LLM and MCP gateway known for its performance and plugin-based extensibility. It handles proxying, routing, load balancing, health checks and authentication.

For AI traffic it adds multi-LLM support, semantic security, and MCP traffic security and analytics. It runs natively on Kubernetes through its official Ingress Controller, and Kong Konnect offers a cloud-hosted version with a free trial.
kong-gateway.who: Platform and API teams that need a single gateway for regular APIs, LLM traffic and MCP servers, self-hosted or in the cloud.
features: API, LLM and MCP gateway in one
Proxying, routing, load balancing and authentication
Kubernetes Ingress Controller; cloud-hosted Kong Konnect

long: AstrBot is an open-source, all-in-one agent chatbot platform that connects to major messaging apps. It is used to build personal AI companions, customer-service bots, automation assistants and knowledge bases.

It supports QQ, WeChat Work, Feishu, DingTalk, WeChat Official Accounts, Telegram, Slack and more, and integrates with agent platforms such as Dify, Alibaba Cloud Bailian and Coze. It has a web UI, over 1,000 one-click plugins and an agent sandbox for isolated code execution.
astrbot.who: Developers and teams who want to run an LLM-powered agent bot inside chat apps like Telegram, Slack, QQ or WeChat.
features: Connects to QQ, WeChat Work, Feishu, DingTalk, Telegram, Slack and more
LLM chat, multimodal input, agents, MCP, skills and knowledge base
Integrates with Dify, Bailian and Coze
Agent sandbox for isolated code and shell execution
Web UI and web chat UI

long: DeepTutor is an open-source AI tutoring system from HKUDS (University of Hong Kong Data Science Lab) aimed at lifelong, personalized learning. It is built with Python and Next.js and has an accompanying arXiv paper.
Recent releases add reading and listening tools, question-bank practice, knowledge bases built on LightRAG, document and video reading, a task board and a learning journal.
deeptutor.who: Students and self-learners who want an AI tutor that works from their own materials, and researchers interested in AI tutoring systems.
features: Personalized tutoring from your own documents
CLI and web app (Python and Next.js)

long: OpenViking is an open-source context database for AI agents: one filesystem for an agent's knowledge, memory and skills. Context is organized as a virtual filesystem under viking:// that agents navigate with ls, tree, read, write and grep.

You can open any directory to inspect and edit what an agent knows. Each directory has a generated summary, and semantic search can be scoped to a project or memory subtree instead of a flat vector pool. A browser-based Studio is available, and it can be self-hosted.
openviking.who: Developers building agents who want inspectable, editable long-term memory and knowledge instead of an opaque vector store.
features: Virtual filesystem (viking://) for knowledge, memory and skills
Agents use ls, tree, read, write and grep
Semantic search scoped to a subtree

facts.license: the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

long: Novu is open-source communication infrastructure for products and AI agents. One API and one conversation model connect to in-app inbox, email, SMS, push, chat, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram and more.
For products it handles notifications with workflows, digests and an embeddable inbox component. Its Agent Communication Infrastructure connects agents you have already built to those channels.
novu.who: Developers who need to send notifications from their product, or connect an AI agent to users over email, chat, SMS and other channels.
features: One API for inbox, email, SMS, push and chat
Slack, Microsoft Teams and Telegram channels
Agent Communication Infrastructure for AI agents

long: DSPy is a framework for programming, rather than prompting, language models. You write compositional Python code to build modular AI systems, from classifiers to RAG pipelines and agent loops.
It includes algorithms that optimize your prompts and weights, so the model learns to produce high-quality outputs. DSPy stands for Declarative Self-improving Python.
dspy.who: Developers and researchers building LLM pipelines who want to replace brittle hand-written prompts with code that can be optimized automatically.
features: Declarative Python modules instead of hand-written prompts
Works for classifiers, RAG pipelines and agent loops
Open source with an active community

long: Lightpanda is a headless browser built from scratch for AI agents and automation. It is not a Chromium fork or a WebKit patch: it is a new browser written in Zig.

In the maker's benchmark of 100 real pages on an AWS m5.large instance, it used about 123 MB of peak memory against 2 GB for headless Chrome and finished in 5 seconds against 46. Nightly builds are available for Linux and macOS on x86_64 and aarch64, and through Homebrew and the AUR.
lightpanda.who: Developers running browser automation, scraping or AI agents at scale who want a lighter, faster headless browser than Chrome.
features: Headless browser written from scratch in Zig
Much lower memory use than headless Chrome in the maker's benchmark
Built for AI agents and automation
Linux and macOS builds (x86_64 and aarch64)
Available via Homebrew and the AUR

facts.license: the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

long: ChatDev began as a multi-agent "virtual software company" in which agents such as a CEO, CTO and programmer design, code, test and document software together. That classic version (1.x) is maintained on its own branch.

ChatDev 2.0 (DevAll), released in January 2026, is a zero-code multi-agent orchestration platform: you define agents, workflows and tasks through configuration rather than code. The team's paper on multi-agent collaboration through evolving orchestration was accepted at NeurIPS 2025.
chatdev.who: Researchers and builders exploring multi-agent systems who want to set up agent teams and workflows by configuration instead of code.
features: Define agents, workflows and tasks by configuration

long: Tabby is a self-hosted AI coding assistant, offered as an open-source, on-premises alternative to GitHub Copilot. It is self-contained, with no need for a database or cloud service.

It has an OpenAPI interface for integrating with existing infrastructure such as cloud IDEs, supports consumer-grade GPUs, and adds features such as a chat side panel, an answer engine and indexing of GitLab merge requests as context.
tabby.who: Engineering teams that want Copilot-style code completion and chat on their own hardware, without sending code to a third-party cloud.
features: No database or cloud service required
IDE extensions with chat side panel
Repository and merge-request indexing for context

long: CloakBrowser is a stealth Chromium build for browser automation. Instead of patching config or injecting JavaScript, it modifies fingerprints in Chromium's C++ source, so anti-bot systems see an ordinary browser.

It works as a drop-in replacement for Playwright and Puppeteer in Python and JavaScript, installs with pip or npm, and has a humanize option for human-like mouse, keyboard and scrolling. A free binary is available, with a paid Pro tier.
cloakbrowser.who: Developers whose scrapers or browser agents get blocked by bot detection and who already use Playwright or Puppeteer.
features: Drop-in Playwright and Puppeteer replacement (Python and JavaScript)
pip install cloakbrowser or npm install cloakbrowser
Free binary plus a paid Pro tier

long: code-review-graph builds a local knowledge graph of your codebase with Tree-sitter, keeps it updated incrementally, and serves compact review context to AI coding tools over MCP, so the assistant reads only the files a change touches.

Its install command detects your AI coding tools and writes an MCP server entry for each, with support for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Continue, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot and others. It requires Python 3.10 or later and also ships a GitHub Action.
code-review-graph.who: Developers using AI coding assistants on large codebases who want more precise, cheaper code reviews.
features: Local code graph built with Tree-sitter
Auto-configures Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed and more

long: ScrapeGraphAI is a Python web-scraping library that uses LLMs and graph logic to build scraping pipelines for websites and local documents such as XML, HTML, JSON and Markdown. You say what information you want and it extracts it.

It has Python and Node SDKs, an API, an MCP server, and integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Agno and low-code tools such as Zapier, n8n and Dify. A hosted version is offered at ScrapeGraphAI.com.
scrapegraphai.who: Developers who want to extract structured data from websites or documents by describing what they need, instead of writing selectors.
features: Works on websites and local XML, HTML, JSON and Markdown
Python and Node SDKs, API and MCP server
Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, n8n, Zapier and Dify
Open source (MIT) with a hosted service

long: MCP for Blender (formerly blender-mcp) connects Blender to any LLM through the Model Context Protocol, for prompt-assisted 3D modeling, scene creation and manipulation. It is a third-party integration, not made by Blender.

One setup command installs the Blender add-on and configures MCP clients it finds on your machine, such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and OpenCode. The PyPI package is now mcp-for-blender, and existing blender-mcp setups keep working.
mcp-for-blender.who: 3D artists and hobbyists who want to build and edit Blender scenes by chatting with an AI assistant.
features: Connects Blender to LLMs over MCP
One-command setup of the add-on and MCP clients
Works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and OpenCode

long: XiaoZhi is an open-source, MCP-based voice chatbot for ESP32 hardware. It uses large models such as Qwen and DeepSeek and controls multiple devices through the MCP protocol.

It supports Wi-Fi, Ethernet and 4G networking, offline wake words with ESP-SR, WebSocket or MQTT plus UDP transports, streaming speech recognition, LLM and text-to-speech pipelines, speaker recognition, and displays and cameras on supported boards. It requires ESP-IDF 6.0.1 or later.
xiaozhi-esp32.who: Makers and hardware hobbyists who want to build their own AI voice assistant device on ESP32 boards.
features: Voice chatbot firmware for ESP32 boards
Offline wake word with customizable wake words
Streaming ASR + LLM + TTS and realtime voice models
Speaker recognition, displays and camera input

long: Supermemory is a memory and context engine for AI. It learns from conversations, extracts facts, builds user profiles, handles updates and contradictions, and forgets expired information, so an AI keeps context between conversations.

It combines memory with full RAG, connectors (Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive and GitHub) and extractors for PDFs, images, video and code. It can give coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode persistent memory, and can be self-hosted.
supermemory.who: Developers adding long-term memory and personalization to AI apps or agents, and people who want their coding assistants to remember past work.
features: Fact extraction with handling of updates and contradictions
Hybrid search across memory and documents
Connectors for Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive and GitHub
PDF, image, video and code extractors
Plugins for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode; self-hostable

long: Repomix packs an entire code repository into a single, AI-friendly file, so you can feed your codebase to LLMs and AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Perplexity and Gemini.
It is distributed on npm and can also be used online at repomix.com.
repomix.who: Developers who want to give a chat assistant or LLM the full context of a codebase in one file.
features: Packs a whole repository into one AI-friendly file
Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek and other LLMs

long: Taskmaster is a task management system for AI-driven development. It breaks work into structured tasks with dependencies and is designed to work with AI chat and coding tools, starting with Cursor and Claude.

It runs as a CLI and as an MCP server (with one-click install for Cursor), supports multiple AI providers through your own API keys, and adds commands for research, tags and workstreams, and team collaboration.
task-master.who: Developers using AI coding agents who want them to plan and work through a structured task list instead of ad-hoc prompts.
features: Works with multiple AI providers via your own API keys
Research and loop commands, tags and workstreams

long: Kilo Code is an open-source AI coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the command line. You choose from 500+ models, can switch between them mid-task, and pay the model provider's rate with no markup.
It installs as a VS Code extension or JetBrains plugin, or you run kilo in any project directory from the terminal.
kilo-code.who: Developers who want an open-source coding agent across VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal with free choice of models at provider pricing.
features: VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin and CLI

long: Go Micro is a Go framework for distributed systems, providing RPC, service discovery, messaging, storage and configuration. Each component is a Go interface with a default implementation you can replace.

It now also treats services as tools for agents: it includes agents (models, conversation history, tools and execution), workflows with retries and checkpoints, and a gateway that exposes services over HTTP and MCP.
go-micro.who: Go developers building microservices who want to expose them to AI agents, or add agents and workflows to an existing service architecture.
features: RPC with streaming, encoding and service discovery
Agents with models, history and tools
Workflows with ordered steps, retries and checkpoints
Gateway exposing services over HTTP and MCP

long: Opik is an open-source LLM observability and evaluation platform from Comet, for AI agent tracing, LLM evaluation, prompt management and production monitoring.
It is Apache-2.0 licensed and the full platform is free to self-host. It includes a client SDK for logging traces and LLM-as-a-judge evaluations; Comet also offers a hosted version.
opik.who: Teams building LLM apps and agents who need to trace calls, evaluate output quality and monitor production, with the option to self-host.
features: Tracing for LLM calls and AI agents
Free to self-host (Apache-2.0); hosted option by Comet

long: Guidance is a programming paradigm for steering language models. It lets you control how output is structured and get high-quality results while reducing latency and cost compared with conventional prompting or fine-tuning.
It offers a Pythonic interface to LLMs, installs from PyPI, and supports backends such as Transformers, llama.cpp and OpenAI, with a richer widget in Jupyter notebooks.
guidance.who: Python developers who need structured, constrained output from language models, such as JSON or specific formats.
features: Backends: Transformers, llama.cpp, OpenAI and more

long: FunASR is an industrial speech-recognition toolkit from ModelScope for offline, streaming and edge deployment.

It covers speech recognition, voice activity detection, punctuation, speaker pipelines and emotion and audio-event models, and can serve models through an OpenAI-compatible API. Fun-ASR-Nano can also run through Hugging Face Transformers.
funasr.who: Developers building voice agents or transcription features who want self-hosted speech recognition, including streaming and edge setups.
features: Speech recognition for offline, streaming and edge use
Hugging Face Transformers quickstart and Colab notebook

long: Agent Zero is an open agent framework for work that needs more than chat. It gives the agent a Dockerized Linux desktop, a browser with DOM annotation, live document co-editing, projects, skills and plugins, and a bridge back to your host machine.
Its plugin hub offers 100+ community plugins, and the agent can use real GUI software, terminals and files inside its desktop.
agent-zero.who: Builders and power users who want a general-purpose, self-hosted agent that can operate a full computer environment.
features: Dockerized Linux desktop for the agent
Live co-editing of Markdown, documents, spreadsheets and presentations

long: Moli is a headless browser for AI agents. Its on-demand layout and rendering design combines a complete browser runtime with a lightweight resource footprint.

It helps agents fetch and extract web pages (as Markdown or a compact semantic tree), search the web and automate browser tasks. You can drive it through its CLI, CDP, WebDriver Classic or WebDriver BiDi on Linux, macOS and Windows.
moli.who: Developers building agents that need to read and automate web pages with less overhead than a full desktop browser.
features: Headless browser built for AI agents
Page extraction as Markdown or a semantic tree
CLI, CDP, WebDriver Classic and WebDriver BiDi

long: Hermes WebUI is a lightweight, dark-themed browser interface for Hermes Agent, the autonomous agent from Nous Research that runs on your server.

It aims for full parity with the Hermes CLI and is built with plain Python and vanilla JavaScript, with no build step. The layout has sessions on the left, chat in the center and workspace files on the right, plus a control center for settings and password protection.
hermes-webui.who: People running Hermes Agent on a server who want to use it from a web browser instead of the terminal.
features: Browser UI with full CLI parity for Hermes Agent
Three-panel layout: sessions, chat and workspace files
Python and vanilla JS, no build step

long: OpenWorker is an open-source AI coworker that runs on your desktop and aims to deliver finished work, such as reviewed code with fixes, polished documents or drafted Slack replies, rather than just chat. It is in open beta.
It doesn't lock you into one model: bring your own API key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or an open-weight provider, or run fully locally with Ollama.
openworker.who: People who want a desktop AI assistant that completes everyday tasks with their choice of model, including fully local models.
features: Desktop AI coworker that completes tasks
Bring your own key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others
Integrations you choose; data stays on your machine otherwise

long: RocketRide describes itself as an open-source AI Development Environment: it turns your IDE, or the CLI, into a place to compose, debug, observe and deploy AI runtimes.

Under the hood it is a data-pipeline builder and runtime for AI and ML workloads, with 100+ pipeline nodes spanning 15+ LLM providers, 9 vector databases, OCR and NER. Pipelines are portable JSON and can be built visually.
rocketride.who: Developers building AI data pipelines and RAG workloads who want to design and run them from their editor.
features: Pipeline builder and runtime for AI and ML
100+ nodes: 15+ LLM providers, 9 vector databases, OCR and NER
Pipelines as portable JSON, built visually
Works inside your IDE or from the CLI

long: Browser Use Web UI is a Gradio interface for browser-use, the library that makes websites accessible to AI agents. It supports most browser-use features in a user-friendly UI.
It works with models from Google, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Ollama and others, can use your own browser so you stay logged in to sites, and supports high-definition screen recording.
browser-use-web-ui.who: People who want to try or run browser-use agents through a web interface instead of writing code.
features: Supports Google, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Ollama models
Use your own browser and logins

long: Framelink MCP for Figma gives Cursor and other AI coding tools access to your Figma files through the Model Context Protocol, so they can implement designs in any framework.

You paste a link to a Figma file, frame or group into your IDE's chat; the server fetches the metadata from the Figma API and simplifies it to the most relevant layout and style information before passing it to the model.
framelink-figma-mcp.who: Front-end developers who build UIs from Figma designs and use Cursor or another AI coding tool.
features: Works with Cursor and other AI coding tools
Paste a Figma link to implement a design
Simplifies Figma API responses to relevant layout and styles

long: Outlines is a library for structured outputs from LLMs, made by the team at .txt. It makes models generate output that follows a schema or format you define.

Its README lists examples such as customer-support triage, e-commerce product categorization and parsing event details. It is trusted by projects including NVIDIA, Cohere, Hugging Face and vLLM, according to its maker.
outlines.who: Developers who need LLM output that reliably matches a JSON schema, type or grammar.
features: Structured generation that follows a schema

long: Midscene.js brings AI vision to end-to-end testing for web, mobile and desktop apps. You describe UI steps and expected results in natural language, and its visual GUI agent carries them out and checks what users see.
You can write YAML test cases with Midscene Test or call its agent APIs from existing Playwright tests, and review HTML reports with screenshots, actions and assertion results.
midscene-js.who: QA engineers and developers who want to write end-to-end tests in plain language instead of brittle selectors.
features: Visual GUI agent for web, mobile and desktop
YAML test cases with Midscene Test
HTML reports with screenshots and assertions

long: Orke is a desktop workspace from BOMTOBE for AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. You give an agent work in a terminal session, then check the result in a web window and a Git window on the same screen, and pick the same session up again from the iPhone or Android app.

It also has "AI employees": you set a goal with the AI in a meeting, and the employee works on its own at scheduled times, leaves anything only a person can do (such as logins or payments) as a request, and records what it did in a log. Orke itself is free; you sign in to Claude Code, Codex or other AI services separately.
orke.who: Developers who already use terminal coding agents like Claude Code or Codex and want sessions, a browser the agent can work in, and Git review in one desktop app.
features: Persistent terminal sessions for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Antigravity and NVIDIA agents; plain terminals work without an AI account
Web window: pick an element on a real page and send it to the agent; agents can also drive the page through Orke browser commands
Git window: diffs, staging, commits, fetch/pull/push, branches, tags and stashes
AI employees that work on a schedule toward a goal, ask a person for logins or payments and keep a work log
Orke CLI so agents can manage sessions, web windows and packages themselves
Continue the same session from the iPhone and Android apps; Linux server mode opens in a browser; optional Docker-compatible isolated environment
Windows (Microsoft Store), macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon (DMG on GitHub Releases), Linux servers (x86_64)
faq: Which platforms does Orke run on?

Windows x64 from the Microsoft Store, macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon (DMG from GitHub Releases), and Linux servers (x86_64), which you use from a browser. There are companion iPhone and Android apps for continuing sessions.
Does Orke include AI model access?
No. Each agent CLI and AI service account is set up and signed in separately, and usage counts toward that account. Regular terminals work without an AI account.

pricing_v.note: AI services such as Claude Code or Codex are used through your own accounts and plans.

long: Agent Resource Market is a beta from Eellos LLC (Texas) where AI agents, not people, are the users. Agents search a public directory of resource offers (data, digital assets, API access, compute, services or authorized actions), publish their own offers, hold structured discussions about a need, and post reviews tied to a specific exchange.

It is API-first: public reads need no account, while writes need an agent key and acceptance of the published rules. Exchanges between agents are simulated: prices and settlement use DEMO_CREDITS, real-money payments are disabled, and the platform does not run or verify what an offer describes. Registration is open but capacity-limited, so check the status endpoint before joining.
agent-resource-market.who: Developers building agents that should find or offer resources from other agents, who want to try an early agent-to-agent directory with a documented HTTP API.
features: Public discovery search over agent profiles, offers and discussions (GET /api/discovery?q=...), with stable crawlable pages
Agents publish offers with input/output schemas and an expected receipt
Structured discussion threads to describe a need or propose a solution
Participant-only simulated exchanges using DEMO_CREDITS; no money moves
Contextual reviews, with buyer and seller ratings kept separate from unverified community opinions
Documented HTTP API (OpenAPI spec), an agent manifest at /.well-known/agent.json and a status endpoint for registration limits
Agent self-registration with Ed25519 proof of key possession; capacity-limited during the beta
faq: Can agents pay each other real money?
No. Payments are disabled in the beta. Exchange prices and settlement states use DEMO_CREDITS, and no money moves.
Does it support MCP or A2A?
The site says the beta implements its own documented HTTP APIs and does not claim MCP or A2A compatibility.
Can anyone register an agent?
Agent self-registration is open, subject to available places. The site's status endpoint shows the current limit.

tiers: Simulated exchanges with DEMO_CREDITS; real-money payments disabled
pricing_v.note: Registration is capacity-limited during the beta.

long: CEOFans is an AI employee and task-management platform from Shanghai Yichong Technology for OPC (one-person company) founders, solo operators and small teams. You pick AI "digital employees" by role (marketing, content, sales, data, engineering and more), give each an identity, a department and task permissions, then delegate tasks and review what comes back.

The work itself runs in a desktop AI agent on your own machine. Each digital employee gets its own revocable employee token, which a compatible agent uses to load the employee's skills, pick up tasks and report logs and results. The site says Codex and Hermes are already connected, and Cursor, Claude Code and OpenClaw can be configured the same way. Approved results are saved as shared company memory or the employee's private memory. The interface is in Chinese.
ceofans.who: Chinese-speaking solo founders, freelancers, independent developers, e-commerce sellers, content creators and small-business owners who already have clear, repeatable tasks and run a desktop coding agent such as Codex.
features: Library of ready-made AI digital employees you choose by role
Departments, identities and task permissions for each digital employee
One revocable employee token per digital employee for desktop agents
Works with Codex and Hermes; Cursor, Claude Code and OpenClaw can be configured
Task system with logs and a review step before results are accepted
Shared company memory and private per-employee memory
Skills library and MCP tool access for compatible desktop agents
faq: Is CEOFans in English?
No. The website and app interface are in Chinese.
Does CEOFans run the AI models itself?
No. Tasks run in a compatible desktop agent such as Codex or Hermes on your machine, using an employee token; model and third-party tool costs are billed separately.

tiers: ¥398/year; 3 AI digital employees, 1 department, 5 GB team memory
¥1,314/year; 10 AI digital employees, 5 departments, 3 human sub-accounts
pricing_v.note: Prices are in Chinese yuan. Model, third-party tool and human review costs are charged separately.

long: 9bot is a WhatsApp automation platform from Brazil for people who run groups, communities and Channels: creators, news portals, educators and companies. It sends recurring messages and news from RSS feeds and APIs, answers custom commands, welcomes new members and posts to WhatsApp Channels, with live-stream alerts for Twitch, YouTube and Kick and scheduled affiliate posts for Mercado Livre, Amazon and Shopee.

Moderation rules handle spam, suspicious links, banned words and a configurable punishment ladder, and a dashboard reports engagement, peak activity and growth. Its official MCP server (remote, OAuth sign-in with your WhatsApp number) lets compatible AI assistants and agents manage groups, schedule messages, moderate and read metrics for your 9bot account. An active 9bot subscription is required.
9bot.who: Admins of busy WhatsApp groups and communities, such as creators, news sites, course providers and community teams, who want moderation, scheduled content and reporting handled automatically, and optionally run from an AI assistant over MCP.
features: Recurring messages, automatic replies and custom commands for WhatsApp groups
Moderation: spam and suspicious-link rules, banned words, punishment ladder
Automatic news delivery from RSS feeds and external APIs
WhatsApp Channel posts, welcome messages and message scheduling
Live-stream alerts (Twitch, YouTube, Kick) and scheduled affiliate posts
Engagement, activity and growth reports in a dashboard
Official remote MCP server (OAuth) for AI assistants and agents
faq: Does 9bot have an MCP server?
Yes. The official remote MCP endpoint is https://mcp.9bot.com.br/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0). You sign in with the WhatsApp number on your 9bot account, and an active subscription is required.
Which languages is 9bot available in?
The site is available in English, Portuguese, Spanish and Chinese.

tiers: Test the full plan before paying
for the first 3 months, then US$70/month; all features included
pricing_v.note: Cancel anytime, according to the pricing section.

long: Pragor is a coordination and governance layer for teams of people and AI agents, not an autonomous agent itself. Each project gets one shared board with tasks that have a real lifecycle and evidence, directed and broadcast messages, approvals, files, a calendar and an attributable activity record of who did what, when and why. Agents built with CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen or your own code connect over a REST API or project-scoped MCP access with a project key; people work in the web UI.

Supported tools can be gated behind a human approval before risky work proceeds, board roles set who can read, contribute and approve, and decisions and evidence stay with the task. Board state, onboarding briefs and history survive session ends, and an optional runner can wake headless agents on a schedule. A read-only live demo board is at pragor.net/demo.
pragor.who: Teams that run several AI agents, often from different frameworks or models, alongside the people accountable for the work, and need approvals for risky actions, clear board permissions and an attributable record.
features: Shared project board: tasks with lifecycle, dependencies and evidence; directed and broadcast messages; files and a calendar
Approval workflows that gate supported tools behind a human decision
Attributable activity record and audit trail of who did what, when and why
Roles and permissions for who can read, contribute and approve, per board
Agents connect over a REST API or project MCP access; works with CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, LangChain or custom code and any model
Board state, briefs and history that persist across agent sessions
Optional agent runner, signed webhooks to Slack and n8n, encrypted per-project keystore
faq: Is Pragor an AI agent?

No. Pragor is a coordination layer: it gives the agents and people on a project one board for tasks, messages, approvals, files and an attributable activity record. Your agents, built with any framework or model, connect to it over REST or project MCP access.
Is Pragor free?

Yes. The public beta is free with no card required (3 projects, 10 agents, unlimited activity events, up to 3 people). There is also a permanent Free plan with narrower limits (1 project, 3 agents, 100 activity events a month, up to 2 people). Paid Solo, Team and Business plans are listed but open after the beta.
Can I try Pragor without signing up?
Yes. A read-only live demo board is at https://pragor.net/demo.

tiers: free while the beta runs, no card: 3 projects, 10 agents, unlimited activity events, 100 MB storage, up to 3 people
permanent plan: 1 project, 3 agents, 100 activity events/month, 100 MB storage, up to 2 people
opens after the beta: 1 project, 10 agents, 3,000 events/month, approvals, calendar, QA
opens after the beta: up to 5 projects, 25 agents, 20,000 events/month, tool registry
opens after the beta: up to 25 projects, unlimited agents, 100,000 events/month
pricing_v.note: Paid plans can't be bought yet; prices shown are list prices (a 25% launch discount is advertised). Reads are always free; the Free plan pauses writes at 100 events until the next month.

long: MailVeri MCP is the official, MIT-licensed Model Context Protocol server for MailVeri, an email verification service. It lets AI assistants such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf and VS Code (Cline) check whether an address is deliverable straight from chat: syntax, MX and SMTP checks, mailbox existence, catch-all domains, disposable providers, role accounts and full inboxes.

Agents can also queue bulk lists for background verification, follow batch progress, download filtered results and check the remaining credit balance before a large outreach run. It runs locally over stdio (or SSE) via uvx from GitHub with a MailVeri API key; verification uses pay-as-you-go credits.
mailveri-mcp.who: Developers, growth and sales teams who clean lead and contact lists, and builders of outreach agents who want their AI assistant to verify emails before sending.
features: Single-email verification: syntax, MX, SMTP, catch-all, disposable, role-account and full-inbox detection
Bulk list verification as background batches, with progress and filtered CSV or ZIP results
Credit balance check before large runs
Six MCP tools (verify_email, verify_batch, get_batch_status, download_batch_result, delete_batch, get_balance)
Configs for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code (Cline) and more; stdio or SSE transport
MIT-licensed server, launched with uvx from GitHub
faq: What does MailVeri MCP cost?

The MCP server is free and open source (MIT). Verifications use MailVeri credits: 1,000 free on sign-up, then pay-as-you-go packs from $9 for 10,000 credits, with no subscription and credits that never expire.
Which AI assistants does it work with?
Any MCP client. MailVeri documents setups for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Antigravity, OpenCode, Pi, Oh My Pi and VS Code (Cline).

pricing_v.note: No subscription; credits never expire.

long: Magpie, from developer yetone, is a free, open-source app that lets every coding agent on your machine use any model. It runs one local gateway (127.0.0.1:3425) that speaks the OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini APIs and translates between them, including streaming, tool calls and reasoning, so Codex can run on DeepSeek or Claude Code on Kimi.

From a menu bar app, window, TUI, web UI or CLI you add providers once (API keys, local models via Ollama, or the Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini or Grok plans you are already signed in to) and pick a model per agent; Magpie edits only the relevant key in each agent's own config. Routing groups fail over to the next account or model when a quota runs out, and profiles switch every agent at once.
magpie.who: Developers who use more than one coding agent, provider or subscription and want to switch models per agent from one place, or keep working when a plan's quota runs out.
features: One local gateway for OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini APIs, with translation between them
Pick a model per agent for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor CLI and 60+ more
Reuse signed-in Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini or Grok plans across agents
Routing groups that fail over when a quota runs out
Menu bar app, TUI, web UI and CLI on macOS, Windows, Linux, Docker and Termux
faq: Does Magpie read my agents' sign-ins?

Yes, to offer the subscriptions your agents are signed in to as providers it reads their sign-ins (for example Claude Code's and Codex's files or the Keychain). You can turn this off in Settings → Privacy → Subscription accounts or with magpie accounts discovery off; API-key providers work either way.
How do I install Magpie?
Download the app from usemagpie.ai, run curl -fsSL https://usemagpie.ai/install.sh | sh, use go install github.com/yetone/magpie@latest, or run the Docker image.

long: OpenFilm is an open-source AI video agent toolkit: install it as a skill (npx skills add openfilm/openfilm) and Claude Code, Codex or any coding agent can make a film. The agent writes the film as web pages, where each shot is a page that draws any moment with one frame(t) function using CSS, SVG, canvas, WebGL, three.js or video, and film.html cuts the pages, footage, pictures and sound together on tracks.

Studio, a local editor that runs in your browser (or in the macOS and Windows desktop app, with a chat for your agents beside it), shows the film taking shape and lets you change any text, color, element or clip by hand. It renders MP4 up to 4K, GIFs, transparent video, stems, subtitles and timelines for Final Cut Pro, Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve; generated voice, music, images and video come from services you connect with your own keys.
openfilm.who: People who already use a coding agent and want it to make launch videos, explainers, music videos or edited footage they can then fine-tune by hand, without a video model subscription.
features: Skill and CLI that turn any coding agent into a video agent
Films as plain HTML: one frame(t) function per shot, cut together in film.html
Studio editor to change text, styles, clips and timing by hand
Renders MP4 up to 4K, GIF, transparent video, subtitles and NLE timelines
No account needed; connect ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, fal and others with your own keys
faq: What do I need to run OpenFilm?
Node 22.2+ and ffmpeg on macOS, Windows or Linux; the first run downloads a headless Chromium (about 100 MB). The desktop app bundles ffmpeg and the browser.
Does OpenFilm need an account?
No. Making, editing and rendering films needs no account; generated voice, music, images and video use the services you connect with your own API keys.

long: ComfyUI is an open-source, node-based engine for generating images, video, 3D models and audio. You build a workflow as a graph of nodes, so every model, parameter and step is visible and adjustable, and it natively supports the latest open models such as Wan, LTX and Hunyuan.

Its maker describes it as highly optimized for local consumer hardware, able to run large open models on as little as 4 GB of VRAM and 8 GB of RAM through asynchronous weight streaming. Partner Nodes add closed models such as Nano Banana and Seedance, and Comfy Cloud runs the same workflows on hosted GPUs, with Comfy Agent able to build workflows for you.
comfyui.who: Artists, video creators and technical users who want fine control over open image and video models, on their own GPU or in the cloud.
features: Node-graph workflows for image, video, 3D and audio generation
Native support for new open models (Wan, LTX, Hunyuan and more)
Runs large models on low-VRAM consumer GPUs
Partner Nodes for closed models such as Nano Banana
Comfy Cloud with 900+ pre-installed models and Comfy Agent
faq: Is ComfyUI free?

The desktop app and engine are free and open source under GPL-3.0. Comfy Cloud is paid: Standard $20/mo, Creator $35/mo, Pro $100/mo and Team $700/mo (about 20% less billed yearly), with free trial runs for new users.

facts.license: the GNU General Public License v3.0

tiers: open source, runs on your own GPU
import your own models and LoRAs
pricing_v.note: Enterprise plans are on request.

long: Immich is a high-performance, self-hosted photo and video management app, an open-source alternative to cloud photo services. You run the server yourself and use the web app or the iOS and Android apps, which back up your library automatically, including in the background.
