It uses machine learning for facial recognition and clustering and for smart search by objects, faces, metadata and CLIP descriptions, and adds albums and shared albums, partner sharing, a global map, memories, RAW and Live Photo support, multi-user accounts and OAuth sign-in.
immich.who: People and families who want a private, self-hosted replacement for Google Photos or iCloud Photos with automatic phone backup and AI search.
features: Automatic and background backup from iOS and Android
Smart search by objects, faces, metadata and CLIP
Shared albums, partner sharing, public links and a global map
Multi-user, OAuth, API keys, RAW and Live Photo support
faq: Can I try Immich before installing it?
Yes. The public demo at demo.immich.app uses the login demo@immich.app with the password demo, and the mobile app can point to the same server URL.
Does Immich replace a backup?
No. The project warns users to always follow a 3-2-1 backup plan for their photos and videos.

facts.license: the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

long: Penpot is an open-source design and prototyping platform for product teams, used in the browser or self-hosted on your own servers. It works with open standards like SVG, CSS, HTML and JSON, expresses design as code, and offers native design tokens, CSS Grid and Flex layouts and real-time collaboration.
Its official MCP server and open API let AI agents read and edit design files, enabling two-way workflows between design and code, and a plugin system makes the workspace programmable.
penpot.who: Product designers and developers who want a Figma-style tool they can own and self-host, and teams that want AI agents to work directly with design files.
features: Browser-based design and prototyping, or self-hosted
Official MCP server for AI agents
Design tokens as a single source of truth
CSS Grid and Flex layouts that behave like code
faq: Is Penpot free?

Yes. The Professional cloud plan is $0 and fully featured, and the open-source edition can be self-hosted. Unlimited costs $7 per editor a month (capped at $175 a month), Enterprise $25 per member a month, and a Private Server $50k a year.

tiers: fully featured, up to 8 team members
pricing_v.note: Self-hosting the open-source edition is free; non-profit, education and open-source discounts are available.

long: Upscayl is a free and open-source desktop app that enlarges and enhances low-resolution images with AI upscaling models, running on your own computer.

It is available for Linux (AppImage, Flatpak, Snap, DEB, RPM), macOS 12+ (including Homebrew) and Windows 10+, and needs a Vulkan-compatible GPU. A separate paid service, Upscayl Cloud, upscales in the browser with credits.
upscayl.who: Photographers, designers and anyone who wants to upscale images locally for free, or in the cloud without a capable GPU.
features: AI image upscaling on your own computer
Linux, macOS and Windows desktop apps
Upscayl Cloud for upscaling without a local GPU
faq: What hardware does Upscayl need?
A Vulkan-compatible GPU. The project notes that many integrated GPUs do not work.

facts.license: the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

tiers: 300 credits a month, upscales up to 256MP
pricing_v.note: Cloud credits are also sold as one-time packs.

long: PhotoPrism is an AI-powered, privacy-first app for browsing, organizing and sharing photos and videos, self-hosted or in the cloud. It automatically labels pictures by content and location and recognizes the faces of family and friends.

It handles RAW images and many video formats, offers combinable search filters (labels, location, resolution, color, quality), Live Photos, maps and places, and runs as an installable progressive web app on phones, tablets and desktops. A public demo is at try.photoprism.app.
photoprism.who: Privacy-minded people who want to keep their photo library on their own hardware while still getting automatic tagging, face recognition and maps.
features: Automatic labels by content and location
RAW and video support, Live Photos
faq: Is PhotoPrism free?

The Community edition is free and open source (AGPL-3.0). Essentials (€2/mo) and Plus (from €6/mo) memberships add features such as extra user roles and 3D maps, and fully managed hosting is available through PikaPods from $6.50/mo.

facts.license: the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

tiers: extra user roles, 3D and satellite maps

long: FastGPT, from Labring (the Sealos team), is an AI agent building platform with ready-made data processing and model calling, plus a visual Flow editor for orchestrating workflows into complex applications such as knowledge-base question answering.

You can self-host it with Docker or use the FastGPT cloud. The source is under the FastGPT Open Source License (Apache 2.0 with extra conditions): commercial use as a backend is allowed, but running a multi-tenant SaaS like FastGPT or removing its logo needs a commercial licence.
fastgpt.who: Teams that want to build RAG knowledge-base assistants and workflow agents visually, self-hosted or as a cloud service.
features: Knowledge bases with data processing and indexing
faq: Can I use FastGPT commercially?
Yes as a backend service or internal platform; a multi-tenant SaaS similar to FastGPT, or removing its logo and copyright notices, requires a commercial licence from the maker.

facts.license: FastGPT Open Source License (Apache 2.0 with additional conditions)

pricing_v.note: Cloud prices in CNY; annual billing gives 12 months for the price of 10. Self-hosted editions are listed separately.

long: Invoke is an open-source creative engine for generating and refining images with AI, with a web-based UI that also underpins several commercial products. It is free to use under a commercially friendly licence and installs on your own hardware through the Invoke launcher.

Its Unified Canvas brings generation, inpainting and outpainting, brush tools and control layers into one space, and node-based Workflows let you build and share custom pipelines. Boards and a gallery keep images and their prompts organized, and a Model Manager handles checkpoints, diffusers and some GGUF models.
invoke.who: Artists and studios who want a polished local app for Stable Diffusion and FLUX image work, with both a canvas and node workflows.
features: Unified Canvas with inpainting, outpainting and control layers
Node-based Workflows you can build and share
Boards and gallery with prompt recall
faq: How do I install Invoke?
Download the Invoke Launcher from GitHub releases and install on compatible hardware.

long: Spleeter is Deezer's open-source source separation library, written in Python on TensorFlow, with pretrained models that split a song into stems: vocals and accompaniment (2 stems), vocals, drums, bass and other (4 stems), or vocals, drums, bass, piano and other (5 stems).

Deezer reports that the 2- and 4-stem models perform strongly on the musdb benchmark and that it can separate audio into 4 stems about 100 times faster than real time on a GPU. It runs from the command line or as a Python library, installs with pip or Docker, and can be used to train your own separation models.
spleeter.who: Musicians, remixers, karaoke and audio developers who need fast, scriptable stem separation.
features: About 100x faster than real time for 4 stems on a GPU
faq: Is Spleeter free for commercial use?
The code is open source under the MIT License.

long: Stability AI is the maker of Stable Diffusion and builds generative models for image, video, 3D and audio, including the Stable Diffusion 3.5 suite, SDXL Turbo, Stable Fast 3D and Stable Audio. You can use the models through its Platform API or self-host them under a licence.

Its open research code, such as the generative-models repository with Stable Video Diffusion and SV4D 2.0, is on GitHub. The Community License lets researchers, developers, small businesses and creators with under $1M in annual revenue use the core models free, while larger companies need an Enterprise licence.
stability-ai.who: Developers and companies that want to build on Stable Diffusion and other Stability models, either via API or self-hosted.
features: Image models (Stable Diffusion 3.5 suite, SDXL Turbo)
Video and 3D models (Stable Video, Stable Fast 3D, SV4D)
Stable Audio for music and sound
faq: Do I have to pay to self-host Stability's models?

Not if you or your organization earn under $1M a year; the Community License covers research, non-commercial and small commercial use. Above that, an Enterprise licence with custom pricing is required.

tiers: commercial use above $1M revenue, implementation support
pricing_v.note: Platform API usage is billed separately; see stability.ai.

long: Ultimate Vocal Remover (UVR) is a free, open-source desktop app that uses state-of-the-art source separation models to remove vocals from audio files or split them into stems. Its core developers, Anjok07 and aufr33, trained all the bundled models except the Demucs v3 and v4 4-stem models.

The installers bundle the interface, Python, PyTorch and other dependencies, so no prerequisites are needed. There are Windows installers (including a DirectML build for AMD Radeon and Intel Arc GPUs), a macOS build and manual install options for Linux.
ultimate-vocal-remover.who: Musicians, DJs, karaoke makers and video editors who want high-quality vocal and instrument separation on their own computer for free.
features: Models trained by the UVR developers plus Demucs
DirectML build for AMD and Intel GPUs
faq: Does UVR need a GPU?
No, but a GPU speeds it up; the Windows DirectML version supports AMD Radeon and Intel Arc cards.

long: AudioCraft is Meta's PyTorch library for deep-learning research on audio generation. It contains inference and training code for MusicGen, a controllable text-to-music model, and AudioGen, a text-to-sound model.

It also includes EnCodec (a high-fidelity neural audio codec), Multi Band Diffusion (an EnCodec-compatible decoder), MAGNeT (non-autoregressive text-to-music and text-to-sound) and AudioSeal for audio watermarking. It installs with pip and needs Python 3.9 and PyTorch 2.1.
audiocraft.who: Researchers and developers who want to generate music or sound effects from text, or train their own audio generation models.
faq: What licence is AudioCraft under?
The code is under the MIT License; the model weights have their own licence, described in the repository.

long: Wan 2.2 is the open, large-scale video generation model family from Alibaba's Wan team, for text-to-video and image-to-video. It introduces a Mixture-of-Experts architecture into video diffusion, separating the denoising process across timesteps with specialized experts to add capacity at the same compute cost.

It was trained on far more data than Wan 2.1 (+65.6% images, +83.2% videos) with curated aesthetic labels for lighting, composition and color, for more controllable cinematic styles. A 5B hybrid text-and-image-to-video model with a high-compression VAE targets high-definition video on consumer GPUs.
wan-2-2.who: Developers, researchers and creators who want to run a state-of-the-art open video model locally or build it into their own tools (it is also supported in ComfyUI).
features: 5B TI2V model with a 16x16x4 compression VAE
Open weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope (Apache-2.0)
faq: Where can I get the Wan 2.2 weights?
From Hugging Face and ModelScope, linked from the GitHub repository.

long: Hunyuan3D is Tencent's family of models for generating 3D assets from images or text, with a shape model that builds the mesh and a paint model that adds high-resolution textures. Tencent also offers it as a free web app.

The Hunyuan3D-2 repository has released turbo and mini shape models, a multiview shape model, a turbo paint model, a Blender add-on and FlashVDM acceleration; Hunyuan3D 2.1 added a fully open PBR material model and training code. The weights are under the Tencent Hunyuan 3D Community License, which does not apply in the EU, UK and South Korea.
hunyuan3d.who: 3D artists, game developers and researchers who want fast image-to-3D or text-to-3D assets, in a browser or on their own GPU.
features: Turbo and mini models for faster generation
faq: Can I use Hunyuan3D in Europe?
The community licence states that it does not apply in the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea.

long: React Doctor, from Million Software, runs deterministic checks on React code written by you or your coding agent and reports issues in state and effects, performance, architecture, security, accessibility and maintainability. It supports projects built with Next.js, Vite, Astro, TanStack, React Native and Expo.

You run a scan with npx react-doctor@latest, install it as a skill so Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or OpenCode can find and fix issues, or add it to CI to report issues each pull request introduces and block merges at a chosen severity. It can also record Chrome DevTools performance traces while you use a running app.
react-doctor.who: React teams and developers whose code is increasingly written by AI coding agents and who want an automated guardrail in the agent loop and in CI.
features: Checks for state/effects, performance, security, accessibility and maintainability
Agent skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenCode
CI mode that blocks regressions in pull requests
faq: Does React Doctor collect data?
The CLI collects crash reports and anonymous usage data; opt out with npx react-doctor@latest --no-telemetry.

long: Botpress is a platform for building and deploying AI agents and chatbots, especially for customer support. You build in Botpress Studio (a visual agent builder) or Viber (a natural-language builder), add knowledge bases, tables and escalation to humans, and deploy to webchat, WhatsApp, Slack and other channels.

Its open-source GitHub repository holds the public integrations on the Botpress Hub and the developer tools (CLI, SDK and API client) for building bots as code. Pricing is per conversation, with AI usage included.
botpress.who: Support and product teams that want AI agents handling customer conversations across channels, and developers extending them with code.
features: Visual Studio and natural-language Viber builders
Knowledge bases, tables and human escalation
Webchat, WhatsApp, Slack and more channels
Integrations with Intercom, Zendesk, HubSpot and Salesforce
CLI, SDK and API client (open source)
faq: Is Botpress free?
There is a free plan with 100 conversations and 3 AI agents. Plus is $150/mo and Team $750/mo (billed annually), with more conversations and AI usage included; Enterprise is custom.

pricing_v.note: Monthly billing costs more; extra conversations are sold in packs of 100.

long: RobotTraining.jobs is a free job board for paid robot-training work: remote robot teleoperation, demonstration and data collection, first-person (egocentric) video capture, robot sensor-data annotation, robot testing and QA, fleet operations, and self-driving vehicle and drone operation. It follows 120 employers and programs, such as Tesla, Figure, Waymo, Zipline and micro1, reads the job boards of the 103 that publish one every day, and shows each role with the hourly pay its posting states and a link to apply on the employer's own site. On Oct 19, 2026 it listed 1,024 open roles.

The same data is open to AI agents. A free remote MCP server at robottraining.jobs/api/mcp (Streamable HTTP, no API key or account) lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Claude Code and other MCP clients search open roles, pull pay by kind of work and read hiring counts by employer, and each returned role links back to apply. The totals and pay figures are also published as JSON and CSV files under a CC BY 4.0 licence, plus a small Python client on PyPI.
robottraining-jobs.who: People looking for paid work teaching or operating robots, and builders who want an AI assistant or agent to answer questions about robot-training jobs, pay and hiring from live, sourced data.
features: Open robot-training roles from 103 employer job boards, re-read daily, with each posting's stated hourly pay
Seven kinds of work: teleoperation, demonstration collection, egocentric capture, embodied-AI annotation, robot QA and evaluation, fleet operations, AV and drone operators
Country filter that hides roles you can't take from where you live
Pay medians and typical ranges per kind of work and per employer, each figure with its source
Free remote MCP server (no key) with three read-only tools
Open data: /roles.json, /pay.json and /pay.csv (CC BY 4.0), an OpenAPI spec and a pip-installable Python client

mcp.auth: None: no API key or account
tools: search_robot_training_jobs
Finds open roles by keyword, kind of work, employer, country or minimum hourly rate (up to 25 results), each with its pay and an apply link.
get_robot_training_pay
Median and typical (25th to 75th percentile) hourly pay per kind of work, shown only when at least three employers post a rate.
get_robot_training_market
How many roles are open now and new in the last 7 days, by kind of work and by employer, optionally for one country.

faq: How do I connect the RobotTraining.jobs MCP server?

In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector and enter https://robottraining.jobs/api/mcp. In Cursor, VS Code or Claude Code, add {"mcpServers": {"robottraining-jobs": {"url": "https://robottraining.jobs/api/mcp"}}} to the MCP config. No key is needed.
Where does RobotTraining.jobs get its pay figures?

From employers' own job postings and pages, read daily. Each figure states its source (a live posting, the employer's statement, an outside report or a labelled estimate), and a market rate is shown only when at least three employers post one. None is a promise of earnings.

tiers: at or under the employer's referral rate
pricing_v.note: Employers pay only for featured roles or for people who onboard; job seekers and AI assistants use it free.

long: Agentic Scientist, from Sakana AI (the team behind The AI Scientist), treats coding agents as AI scientists. You give it a task.md describing a research problem; the agents propose ideas, run experiments, score them against the task rubric and iterate toward stronger programs. The pipeline then runs baselines and ablations, a sealed final evaluation and post-hoc analyses, and writes, compiles and audits a paper against that evidence, with every stage kept under one run directory.

It drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and pi through the Headless CLI, so the same experiment can be repeated across agents and models. Every phase runs in its own Docker container by default, because the agents run with full tool permissions, and a browser-based Run Inspector lets you review each run. The accompanying paper is on arXiv (2610.18933).
agentic-scientist.who: Researchers and ML engineers who want to hand a well-defined research task to coding agents and get back experiments, ablations and a draft paper they can check, and people comparing how different agents and models do on the same task.
features: Six phases: task drafting, investigation, ablations, sealed final evaluation, post-hoc analysis and paper
Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and pi (agent.name=...)
Each phase runs in its own Docker container for safety and reproducibility
Optional external AI review and revision phases for the paper
Run Inspector web UI to browse ideas, attempts, results and the manuscript
CPU-only example task (circle packing) plus GPU task presets
faq: What do I need to run Agentic Scientist?

Docker, Python 3.11+ with uv, and API keys or a subscription for the coding agent you pick (for example a Claude login for the default claude agent). GPUs are only needed for the GPU task presets; the circle-packing example runs on CPU.
Is it safe to run?

The project warns that it launches coding agents with full tool permissions, so they can run arbitrary commands. It recommends keeping runs inside its Docker image, only running tasks and sources you trust, and reviewing run directories before sharing them.

long: OpenGCUA (Open Generalist CUA) is an ongoing open project from the MAI-UI team at Tongyi Lab to build the full stack for generalist computer-use agents: systems that complete computer tasks by deciding for themselves whether to look at a screenshot or an accessibility tree, and whether to click, call an API, run a shell command or write a small program that combines them.

The first research preview (October 2026) releases an OSWorld integration example with reference screenshot-action and code-action agents, evaluation trajectories for eight frontier models, a preliminary macOS real-device harness (a menu-bar app that runs the agent on your own Mac) and a Cross-Device SDK with one programming interface for computers, browsers and phones. On the OSWorld-v2 offline set the team reports the design raised the mean partial score of the eight models from 45.3 to 64.9 and cut steps per task by 53% on average. A model release is listed as next on the roadmap.
opengcua.who: Researchers and developers building computer-use agents who want an open harness, SDK and benchmark trajectories to start from, and Mac users who want to try a real-device agent.
features: Generalist design: GUI, accessibility tree, shell, API and code actions in one agent
OSWorld integration example with screenshot-action and code-action agents
Evaluation trajectories of 8 frontier models released
macOS real-device harness (macOS 14+) that can work in background windows
Cross-Device SDK (qwen-intelligence-sdk) for computers, browsers and phones
Interactive lab and tech report on the project site
faq: What does OpenGCUA need to run?
The macOS real-device harness needs macOS 14 or later; Python 3.12 is recommended, and prebuilt SDK wheels do not need Rust. The project calls the harness and SDK preliminary.
Is there an OpenGCUA model?
Not yet. The roadmap lists a GCUA model for computer and browser use as the next release; this preview opens the harness, SDK, OSWorld example and trajectories.

long: llmware is an open-source Python framework for building knowledge-based LLM applications that run locally and privately: on AI PCs and laptops, at the edge or self-hosted, across Windows, Mac and Linux. It supports GGUF, OpenVINO, ONNX Runtime (including Qualcomm QNN), Windows Local Foundry and PyTorch, and picks the right inference technology for the target machine.

It has two parts: a model catalog of 300+ quantized models, including 50+ of llmware's own fine-tuned SLIM, Bling, Dragon and Industry-BERT models for enterprise tasks (cloud models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are supported too), and a RAG pipeline that parses, chunks, embeds and indexes documents into libraries you can query with text, semantic, hybrid and metadata filters and prompt with sources.
llmware.who: Developers building private RAG and agent apps for enterprise documents who want small models that run on a laptop or on-prem hardware instead of a cloud API.
features: Model catalog with 300+ models in optimized, quantized formats
50+ fine-tuned small models (SLIM, Bling, Dragon, Industry-BERT) for RAG and automation
Document parsing, chunking, embedding and knowledge-base libraries
Text, semantic, hybrid and metadata queries, plus prompt-with-sources
Runs on CPU, GPU and NPU via GGUF, OpenVINO and ONNX Runtime
Database options from a laptop to a parallel cluster
faq: Does llmware need a GPU or cloud API?
No. The project says virtually all of its examples and models can run on device, on a laptop, and it is optimized for AI PCs; cloud models are optional.

long: memU is a lightweight, agent-driven memory system from NevaMind AI that gives you one personal memory, stored as a readable Markdown wiki, across sessions, agents and devices. A scheduled background task captures useful knowledge from your agent sessions and distills reusable skills from your agent history, and relevant memory is brought back into later tasks.

It works with Codex and ChatGPT's Work mode, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, WorkBuddy and others on macOS and Windows; setup is a message to your agent pointing it at memU's SKILL.md with an API key from memu.so. The core memory logic is about 500 lines of open-source code, and the hosted cross-device service is described by the maker as free and unlimited.
memu.who: People who use several coding or desktop agents (for example Codex at work and Claude Code at home) and want them to share the same memory of their projects and preferences.
features: One shared memory across agents, sessions and devices
Memory stored as an inspectable Markdown wiki with source-linked recall
Automatic skill extraction from your agent history
Tested adapters for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent and WorkBuddy
Install by sending your agent the SKILL.md link plus an API key
faq: Is memU free?
The open-source code is under the Apache 2.0 License, and the maker describes the hosted cross-device memory at memu.so as free and unlimited (checked Oct 20, 2026).
Which agents are not supported?
The README lists ChatGPT's Chat mode and Claude's Chat and Cowork modes as not supported; use ChatGPT's Work mode or Claude Code instead.

long: Hermes One is a community-maintained, open-source desktop app for installing, configuring and chatting with Hermes Agent, Nous Research's self-improving AI assistant. Instead of managing the command line, it walks you through install (using the official Hermes install script), provider setup and daily use, and can also connect to a remote Hermes API server.

It adds a streaming chat UI with token and cost tracking, 22 slash commands, searchable session history, separate profiles, a memory and persona editor, 14 toolsets, scheduled tasks with a cron builder, and messaging gateways, with providers from OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, xAI and Nous Portal to local Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and llama.cpp. The maker notes it is in active development.
hermes-one.who: People who want to use Hermes Agent with a point-and-click app on Windows, macOS or Linux rather than the terminal.
features: Guided first-run install of Hermes Agent, local or remote backend
Many providers, including local OpenAI-compatible servers
Streaming chat with token usage and cost display
Session search, profiles, memory, persona (SOUL.md) and skills management
Scheduled tasks with 15 delivery targets and messaging gateways
faq: Is Hermes One official?
No. It is a community-maintained app that uses the official Hermes Agent install script; Hermes Agent itself is made by Nous Research.
How do I install Hermes One?
Download the desktop app from hermesone.org or GitHub Releases; the Windows installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first launch.

long: Instructor is a popular open-source library for getting reliable structured output (JSON) from LLMs. You define a Pydantic model, and Instructor handles the schema, validation, parsing and automatic retries, feeding validation errors back to the model until the output fits.

The same code works across major providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others, including local models), with streaming of partial objects and lists, nested models and full type safety and IDE support. Its maintainers suggest Instructor for fast, schema-first extraction and PydanticAI when you need full agent runs.
instructor.who: Python developers who need clean, validated data out of LLM calls for extraction, classification or agent tool inputs.
features: Pydantic models as the output schema
Automatic retries with the validation error fed back
One interface across many LLM providers
faq: Is Instructor free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License; you only pay your model provider.
When should I use PydanticAI instead?
Instructor's README recommends PydanticAI when you need richer agent runs, built-in observability or shareable traces, and Instructor for simple, cheap extraction.

long: TRELLIS is Microsoft's open model for generating 3D assets from text or image prompts. It is built on a unified Structured LATent (SLAT) representation that can be decoded to different formats, including radiance fields, 3D Gaussians and meshes, with rectified-flow transformers as the backbone.

Microsoft released pre-trained models of up to 2 billion parameters trained on a dataset of 500K diverse 3D objects, plus training code, the TRELLIS-500K dataset and Gradio demos. It also supports variants of the same object and local editing of a generated asset. The maintainers recommend generating an image first and using the image model, since the text-conditioned models are less detailed.
trellis.who: 3D artists, game and XR developers and researchers who want to generate textured 3D assets locally from an image or a prompt.
features: Outputs radiance fields, 3D Gaussians or meshes
Models up to 2B parameters, trained on 500K objects
Training code, dataset toolkit and Gradio demos
faq: Is TRELLIS free?
Yes. The code and models are open source under the MIT License.
Should I use text or image prompts?
The project recommends text-to-image first, then the TRELLIS image model, because its text-conditioned models are less creative and detailed.

long: Portkey's AI Gateway is a fast, lightweight open-source gateway that puts hundreds of LLMs behind one API (Portkey cites 250+ LLMs and 1,600+ language, vision, audio and image models). You can integrate a new model in minutes and add reliability without changing app code.

It handles automatic retries and fallbacks, load balancing and conditional routing, guardrails, multimodal requests and agent-framework integrations, and Portkey's MCP Gateway adds enterprise auth and observability for MCP servers. You can self-host the open-source gateway or use Portkey's hosted platform, which adds observability, prompt management and caching; a Gateway 2.0 pre-release is merging Portkey's enterprise gateway into the open-source project.
portkey-ai-gateway.who: Teams running LLM apps or agents in production who want one API across providers, with fallbacks, budgets and logs.
features: One API for hundreds of models and providers
Automatic retries, fallbacks and load balancing
MCP Gateway with auth and observability
Self-host free or use the hosted platform with logs and prompt management
faq: How much does Portkey cost?

The open-source gateway is free to self-host. The hosted Developer plan is free (10k recorded logs a month), Production is $49/month (100k logs, then $9 per extra 100k requests), and Enterprise is custom.

tiers: 10k recorded logs a month, 3-day log retention

long: CogVideoX is a family of open text-to-video and image-to-video models from Zhipu AI (Z.ai) and Tsinghua University's THUDM group, released with inference and fine-tuning code. The CogVideoX1.5-5B models generate 10-second videos at higher resolution, and the image-to-video model works at any resolution.

The smaller models run on consumer GPUs: the README says CogVideoX-2B runs on older cards such as a GTX 1080 Ti and CogVideoX-5B on desktop GPUs such as an RTX 3060. It supports LoRA fine-tuning through diffusers, DDIM inversion, and the CogKit toolkit; online demos are on Hugging Face and ModelScope.
cogvideox.who: Developers, researchers and creators who want to run or fine-tune an open video generation model on their own hardware.
features: LoRA fine-tuning via diffusers, plus CogKit
3D causal VAE and tech report released
faq: What licence does CogVideoX use?
The code is Apache-2.0 and CogVideoX-2B is under the Apache 2.0 License; check each model card on Hugging Face for the 5B models' terms.

long: txtai is an all-in-one open-source Python framework from NeuML for semantic search, LLM orchestration and language-model workflows. Its core is an embeddings database that combines sparse and dense vector indexes, graph networks and relational storage, so it works both as a vector search engine and as a knowledge source for RAG.

On top of that it offers LLM pipelines (prompts, question answering, labeling, transcription, translation, summarization), workflows that chain them, and agents that connect embeddings, pipelines and workflows to solve problems on their own. It exposes web and Model Context Protocol (MCP) APIs, with bindings for JavaScript, Java, Rust and Go, and runs locally or scales out in containers.
txtai.who: Python developers building semantic search, RAG or small agent systems who want one batteries-included library they can run locally.
features: Embeddings database: vector, graph and relational indexes
Vector search with SQL, topic modeling and multimodal indexing
LLM pipelines for QA, summarization, transcription and more
Web and MCP APIs, with JS, Java, Rust and Go bindings
faq: Is txtai free?
Yes, it is open source under the Apache 2.0 License. NeuML, the company behind it, offers paid consulting.

long: Nango is a platform for building product integrations that connects your app and your AI agents to 1,000+ APIs. It gives you three building blocks: managed auth (OAuth, API keys and token refresh, with an embeddable white-label auth flow), a proxy that makes authenticated requests for your users with retries and rate-limit handling, and functions, TypeScript integration logic you write yourself or generate with its AI builder and deploy to Nango's runtime.

Use cases include AI tool calling and MCP, data syncs and webhooks. Nango says it is used in production by Replit, Ramp and Mercor, offers about 7,000 pre-built tools, triggers and syncs, and can be self-hosted on the Enterprise plan; the code is source-available under the Elastic License 2.0.
nango.who: SaaS and AI-agent teams that need their product or agents to act in users' third-party accounts (CRM, email, calendars and more) without building every integration and OAuth flow themselves.
features: Managed auth for 1,000+ APIs and MCP servers
Proxy for authenticated API calls with retries
TypeScript functions for tools, syncs and webhooks, with an AI builder
About 7,000 pre-built tools, triggers and syncs
Logs, OpenTelemetry export, SOC 2 Type II
faq: How much does Nango cost?

Free is $0 with hard-capped monthly limits (10 connections, 10 compute hours, 10 GB). Pay-as-you-go is $50/month including $50 of credits, then $0.29 per connection, $0.72 per compute hour and $0.50 per GB. Enterprise is custom and adds self-hosting.

tiers: 10 connections, 10 compute hours, 10 GB a month (hard caps)
shared Slack channel, faster integration requests

long: HunyuanVideo is Tencent's open video foundation model and framework for text-to-video generation, released with PyTorch model code, pre-trained weights and inference code. At release Tencent described it as the largest open video generation model, with over 13 billion parameters, and reported quality comparable to leading closed models.

It is integrated into Hugging Face Diffusers, has FP8 weights to save GPU memory and parallel inference via xDiT. Tencent has since built a family on it: HunyuanVideo-I2V (image-to-video), HunyuanCustom, HunyuanVideo-Avatar (audio-driven animation) and the newer, more efficient HunyuanVideo-1.5.
hunyuanvideo.who: Researchers, developers and studios who want to run or build on a large open video model on their own GPUs.
features: Weights, inference and parallel inference code
Related I2V, Custom and Avatar models, plus HunyuanVideo-1.5
faq: Can I use HunyuanVideo commercially?
It is released under the Tencent Hunyuan Community License, which does not apply in the European Union, United Kingdom and South Korea; read the licence for its terms before commercial use.

long: Claude Context is an open-source MCP plugin from Zilliz that adds semantic code search to Claude Code and other AI coding agents. It indexes your codebase into a vector database and brings only the relevant code into the agent's context, so the agent finds code across millions of lines without many rounds of file discovery.

Zilliz pitches it as cost-effective for large codebases, since it avoids loading whole directories for every request. It needs a vector database (Milvus or a free Zilliz Cloud cluster) and an embedding provider such as OpenAI, works as an MCP server with Claude Code, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients, and also ships as a VS Code extension and npm packages.
claude-context.who: Developers using Claude Code or another coding agent on large repositories who want better, cheaper code retrieval.
features: Semantic code search over your whole codebase via MCP
Works with Claude Code, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients
Vector storage in Milvus or Zilliz Cloud
VS Code extension and npm core package
Keeps context small to reduce token costs
faq: What does Claude Context need?
A vector database (a free Zilliz Cloud cluster or your own Milvus) and an embedding model API key, for example OpenAI's. The plugin itself is free and MIT-licensed.

long: Inbox Zero is an open-source AI email assistant and email app for Gmail and Outlook. The assistant works in the background: it sorts and labels mail, pre-drafts replies in your tone, follows plain-English rules you write, tracks what needs a reply, blocks cold email, bulk-unsubscribes and archives, files attachments to Google Drive or OneDrive, and sends briefings before meetings.

You can chat with it from Slack or Telegram to manage your inbox on the go. The separate email client offers a split inbox, multiple accounts and team comments, and is free on web, desktop and iPhone. The code can be self-hosted, and the hosted service has paid plans with a 7-day free trial.
inbox-zero.who: Busy founders, executives and teams who get a lot of email and want an assistant that triages and drafts for them, with the option to self-host.
features: Auto-sorting, labeling and drafted replies in your voice
Reply tracking, cold email blocker, bulk unsubscribe and archive
Meeting briefs and auto-filing of attachments
Chat with your inbox from Slack or Telegram
Free email app for web, desktop and iPhone
faq: How much does Inbox Zero cost?

Paid monthly, Starter is $20, Plus $35 and Professional $50 a month; billed yearly they are $18, $28 and $42 per user per month. Each has a 7-day free trial, and Enterprise is by quote. The email app is free.
Can I self-host Inbox Zero?
Yes. The code is open source under the AGPL-3.0, and the docs include a quick start, setup CLI and Docker guide for self-hosting.

facts.license: the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

tiers: sorting, drafted replies, cold-email blocker, analytics
2 email accounts per user, meeting notetaker, Slack, integrations
pricing_v.note: 7-day free trial on each plan; the email app is free; self-hosting the open-source code is free.

long: assistant-ui is an open-source TypeScript/React library for building production-grade AI chat experiences, the UX of ChatGPT in your own app. It gives you composable primitives (Thread, Message, Composer, ThreadList, ActionBar) that you can style yourself or start from a shadcn/ui theme that its CLI copies into your project.

It handles streaming, auto-scroll, retries, attachments, markdown, code highlighting, voice dictation, keyboard shortcuts and accessibility, and supports generative UI: rendering tool calls as React components and collecting inline human approvals. Runtimes connect it to the Vercel AI SDK, LangGraph and LangChain, AG-UI and A2A, Google ADK and others, and it also targets React Native and Ink. Optional assistant-cloud adds hosted thread persistence.
assistant-ui.who: Front-end and full-stack developers adding a chat or agent interface to a React, React Native or terminal app.
features: Composable chat primitives with a shadcn/ui starting theme
Streaming, attachments, markdown, code highlighting and voice dictation
Generative UI: tool calls as components, inline approvals
Runtimes for AI SDK, LangGraph, AG-UI, A2A and more
faq: Is assistant-ui free?
The library is free and MIT-licensed. Optional assistant-cloud is Free (200 monthly active users), Pro $50/month (500 MAU, then $0.10 per extra MAU) or Enterprise custom.

tiers: MIT licence, use your own backend
pricing_v.note: MAU = monthly active users who send at least one message.

long: YuE is an open song-generation project from the Multimodal Art Projection (M-A-P) community; its current version, YuE2, turns lyrics and a style prompt into a complete song with vocals and accompaniment. It first writes an explicit melody-and-chord plan, then renders that plan as audio, so a person or an agent can read, play and change the composition before rendering.

The same model does zero-shot covers of transcribed songs in a new style and agentic editing through a conversation about score, arrangement and lyrics. Its maintainers report it is competitive with Suno v5/v6 on WildSongBench. A yue2-music agent skill teaches agents to generate songs and instrumentals and edit ABC scores, and a free online demo is available.
yue.who: Musicians, producers and developers who want an open, controllable song generator they can run themselves or drive from an AI agent.
features: Lyrics-to-song with vocals and accompaniment, 48 kHz stereo
Editable symbolic plan (melody and chords) before audio
yue2-music agent skill for instrumentals and ABC scores
Free online demo; runs locally on a 24 GB NVIDIA GPU
faq: What hardware does YuE2 need?
Linux, Python 3.12 and an NVIDIA GPU with BF16 support and 24 GB of VRAM; model files download from Hugging Face on first use.
Where is the original YuE?
Its code, documentation and licence are kept on the repository's YuE-v1 branch.

long: OpenUI, from Thesys, is an open-source, framework-agnostic generative UI framework. Its centerpiece is OpenUI Lang, a compact, streaming-first language for model-generated interfaces that, by the maker's figures, uses up to 67% fewer tokens than JSON.

You define the components a model may use, OpenUI generates the prompt instructions from that library, and a streaming renderer draws the UI progressively as tokens arrive. A framework-agnostic core powers runtimes for React, Vue, Svelte and Angular, and React also gets built-in component libraries (charts, forms, tables, layouts) and ready-made chat interfaces. The project notes it has no official cryptocurrency or token.
openui.who: Developers building AI assistants, copilots or agent apps that should answer with real interface elements instead of plain text.
features: OpenUI Lang: compact, streaming-first UI language
Prompt instructions generated from your component library
Streaming renderer for React, Vue, Svelte and Angular
Built-in charts, forms, tables and chat interfaces for React
faq: Is OpenUI free?
Yes, it is open source under the MIT License.

long: MCP Inspector is the official developer tool from the Model Context Protocol project for testing and debugging MCP servers. One npm package, @modelcontextprotocol/inspector, gives you four ways in: a web app, a scriptable CLI for automation and CI, an interactive terminal UI, and an experimental connection CLI (mcpdo) that keeps a named connection open across many commands.

You point it at a server over stdio or HTTP, then list and call its tools, read resources, try prompts and watch the raw protocol messages. It handles OAuth flows and stores tokens and secrets in the OS keychain where one is available, so it is the usual first stop when an MCP server misbehaves in Claude, Cursor or another client.
mcp-inspector.who: MCP server authors and anyone wiring MCP servers into an agent who needs to see exactly what a server exposes and returns.
features: Web UI, CLI, terminal UI and mcpdo connection CLI in one package
Call tools, read resources and test prompts
OAuth support with secrets kept in the OS keychain
faq: Is MCP Inspector free?
Yes. It is open source from the Model Context Protocol project; new code is Apache-2.0 while the project finishes moving off MIT.

facts.license: the Apache License 2.0 (moving from MIT; older contributions stay MIT)

long: RobotGo is a Go library for native desktop automation on macOS, Windows and Linux (x86-64 and arm64). It controls the mouse and keyboard, reads the screen and pixel colours, captures bitmaps, manages processes and window handles, and listens for global input events.

It is used for RPA scripts, GUI test automation and, increasingly, as the low-level action layer for computer-use agents written in Go. The maker also sells RobotGo-Pro, a separate paid edition with JavaScript, Python and Lua bindings and support.
robotgo.who: Go developers building desktop automation, GUI tests or the action layer of a computer-use agent.
features: Screen capture, pixel reading and bitmap search
Global keyboard and mouse event listener
macOS, Windows and Linux, x86-64 and arm64
faq: Is RobotGo free?
The open-source library is free under Apache-2.0. RobotGo-Pro, with extra language bindings and support, is a separate paid product.

long: Tyk Gateway is an open-source API and AI gateway, written in Go, that sits in front of REST, GraphQL, TCP, gRPC and Model Context Protocol (MCP) services. The open-source gateway ships with no feature lockout: rate limiting, authentication, analytics, quotas and microservice patterns are all included.

For agent builders, Tyk adds an MCP gateway and AI gateway so tool and model traffic can be authenticated, governed and metered like any other API. You can run the gateway yourself, buy the self-managed enterprise platform with a dashboard and developer portal, or use the hosted Tyk Cloud.
tyk-gateway.who: Platform teams that already manage APIs and want the same auth, rate limits and analytics on MCP servers and LLM traffic.
features: API gateway for REST, GraphQL, TCP and gRPC
MCP gateway and AI gateway features
Rate limiting, auth, quotas and analytics built in
Self-host open source, self-managed enterprise or Tyk Cloud
faq: Is Tyk Gateway open source?
Yes. The gateway is under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, except its ee folder. The dashboard, developer portal and Tyk Cloud are commercial.

facts.license: the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (except the ee folder)

long: Krita AI Diffusion is a plugin that brings generative image AI into the Krita painting app. Instead of generating whole pictures from a prompt, it focuses on control: you can restrict generation to a selection, refine existing content at a chosen strength, focus text on regions, and guide results with reference images, sketches, line art and depth maps.

It runs on a local ComfyUI backend that the plugin can install for you, so it works offline and free on your own GPU; the maker also offers an optional paid cloud service (Interstice) for people without suitable hardware.
krita-ai-diffusion.who: Illustrators and artists who already paint in Krita and want inpainting, outpainting and guided generation inside their normal workflow.
features: Generate within selections, with adjustable strength
Control with sketches, line art, depth and reference images
Local ComfyUI backend, offline and free
Optional hosted cloud from the maker
faq: Is Krita AI Diffusion free?
The plugin is free and open source (GPL-3.0) and runs locally on your GPU. The maker's optional cloud service is paid.

facts.license: the GNU General Public License v3.0

long: Desktop Commander is an MCP server that lets Claude and other AI clients work directly on your computer: run and manage long-running terminal commands and processes, search the file system, and edit files with search-and-replace diffs. It builds on the reference MCP Filesystem server and adds those editing and process tools.

Because it runs through your existing AI subscription rather than per-token API calls, many people use it as a low-cost coding and automation agent. It also offers a remote MCP endpoint for ChatGPT and Claude on the web, and a file preview and Markdown editor UI.
desktop-commander-mcp.who: People who want Claude Desktop or another MCP client to run commands and edit files on their own machine.
features: Run and manage long-running terminal processes
File system search and diff-based file editing
Remote MCP for ChatGPT and Claude web
File preview UI and Markdown editor
faq: Is Desktop Commander free?
Yes, the MCP server is open source under the MIT License.

long: UFO is Microsoft's open-source framework for agents that operate computers. UFO² is a stable desktop agent OS for Windows that combines GUI actions with native API calls and deep Windows integration, while UFO³ (Galaxy) coordinates many device agents at once.

In Galaxy, a task is broken into a graph of steps (a constellation) that can be edited while it runs, executed in parallel across devices, and coordinated over a unified agent protocol. UFO² can act as one of those device agents.
ufo.who: Researchers and developers building Windows automation or multi-device computer-use agents.
features: UFO² desktop agent for Windows with GUI and API actions
faq: Is UFO free?
Yes, it is open source from Microsoft under the MIT License; you supply the model API.

long: LTX-2 is Lightricks' open-weights audio-video foundation model, a diffusion transformer that generates synchronized video and sound in one model. The repository is the official Python inference package and LoRA trainer, with pipelines for the LTX-2.5 checkpoints published on Hugging Face.

It offers several speed and quality modes, latent upscaling and distilled variants. The full model download is large (around 66 GB for the main set), so it is aimed at people with serious GPUs; Lightricks also offers API access.
ltx-2.who: Developers and studios who want to run or fine-tune an open audio-video generation model on their own hardware.
features: Official inference pipelines and LoRA trainer
faq: Is LTX-2 open source?
The code and weights are openly available under the LTX-2.x Community License, which is not an OSI open-source licence; check its terms for commercial use.

long: Mobile MCP, from Mobile Next, is an MCP server that lets agents drive iOS and Android apps on simulators, emulators and real devices through one platform-neutral interface. Agents read structured accessibility snapshots, or fall back to screenshot-based coordinate taps when needed.

It works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, GitHub Copilot and any other MCP client, and can run against devices on your own machine or real devices in Mobile Next's cloud. Typical uses are app test automation, scripted form flows and multi-step user journeys.
mobile-mcp.who: Mobile developers and QA teams who want an AI agent to test or operate native iOS and Android apps.
features: iOS and Android, simulators, emulators and real devices
Optional real-device cloud from Mobile Next
faq: Is Mobile MCP free?
The MCP server is open source under Apache-2.0. Mobile Next Cloud for remote real devices is a separate service.

long: Windows-MCP is a lightweight open-source MCP server that gives AI agents control of Windows 10 and 11: navigating files, opening and controlling apps and windows, interacting with UI elements, simulating input and running QA tests. It works with any model and does not need computer vision, though vision is optional.
It is distributed on PyPI (uvx windows-mcp), listed in the MCP Registry and as a Claude Desktop extension, where the maker reports more than two million users.
windows-mcp.who: Windows users and developers who want Claude or another MCP client to operate their PC.
features: Native Windows UI interaction and app control
Works with any LLM, vision optional
Install via uvx or Claude Desktop extension
faq: Is Windows-MCP free?
Yes, it is open source under the MIT License.

long: BAML is a programming language from Boundary built for writing agents and LLM functions. It looks like TypeScript but has a strict, Rust-like type system that persists at runtime, typed errors, Go-style concurrency and a built-in test and eval framework, so model outputs are parsed into real types instead of loose strings.
You can run BAML on its own or adopt it gradually, calling BAML functions from TypeScript, Python, Go, C#, Java and other languages, with editor tooling and an agent install command.
baml.who: Developers who want structured, type-safe LLM calls and agent logic that plugs into an existing codebase.
features: Typed language for LLM functions and agents
Runtime types, typed errors, no unsafe casts
Call from TypeScript, Python, Go, C#, Java and more
faq: Is BAML free?
Yes, BAML is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

long: Bifrost, from Maxim AI, is an open-source AI gateway that puts more than 20 providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex and others) behind one OpenAI-compatible API. It starts with one npx or Docker command and includes a web UI for configuration and monitoring.

It adds automatic failover, load balancing, semantic caching, virtual keys and budgets, and also works as an MCP gateway. The maker says it adds under 200 microseconds of overhead at 5,000 requests per second.
bifrost.who: Teams running LLM apps or agents in production who want one fast gateway for routing, failover and spend control.
features: Failover, load balancing and semantic caching
Web UI, runs via npx or Docker
faq: Is Bifrost free?
The gateway is open source under Apache-2.0. Maxim AI sells an enterprise edition and its own evaluation platform.

long: TypeChat is a Microsoft library for building natural-language interfaces with types. Instead of prompt engineering, you define TypeScript (or Python) types that describe the intents your app supports, and TypeChat builds the prompt, validates the model's JSON reply against the schema and asks the model to repair any reply that doesn't fit.
It suits apps such as command interfaces, shopping carts or music players where user requests must become well-formed actions.
typechat.who: Developers who need LLM replies to map reliably onto their app's data types.
features: Schema engineering instead of prompt engineering
Validates model output against your types
faq: Is TypeChat free?
Yes, it is open source from Microsoft under the MIT License.

long: Qwen-Image is the Qwen team's open-weights image generation foundation model, a 20B MMDiT known for unusually accurate text rendering (especially Chinese) and precise image editing. A separate Edit model handles instruction-based edits.

Qwen-Image-2.0, announced in February 2026, adds long-instruction typography for infographics, posters and slides, native 2K resolution and unified generation and editing. Weights are on Hugging Face and ModelScope, and you can try it in Qwen Chat.
qwen-image.who: Designers and developers who want an open image model that can render legible text and edit images precisely.
features: Weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope
Try it free in Qwen Chat
faq: Is Qwen-Image free?
Yes, the weights are released under the Apache License 2.0.

long: The Claude Agent SDK for Python is Anthropic's official library for building agents on the same harness that powers Claude Code. A simple async query() call streams Claude's messages, and a client class supports interactive sessions, custom tools, hooks and permission settings.
The Claude Code CLI comes bundled with the package, so pip install claude-agent-sdk is enough to start (Python 3.10+); you can point it at your own Claude Code install instead.
claude-agent-sdk-python.who: Python developers who want Claude Code's agent loop, tools and permissions inside their own apps and scripts.
features: Official Anthropic SDK for the Claude Code harness
faq: Is the Claude Agent SDK free?
The SDK is free and open source (MIT). You pay for Claude usage through the API or your plan.

long: Repowise indexes your codebase once on your machine (code, call graph, git history, tests, docs and design decisions) so you and your coding agent can ask it what calls what, what breaks if something changes, what code is dead, what to fix first and why it was built that way.

Graph, risk, health, test and dead-code analysis run without LLM calls, so the same diff gives the same answer, and agents reach it through REST and MCP with scoped tokens. It also produces code health scores and docs, and can enforce change policy in CI via SARIF. It is free for one developer; a commercial licence and hosted option cover company use.
repowise.who: Engineers and teams who want their coding agents to stop re-reading the codebase and work from a shared, deterministic index.
features: Local index of code, call graph, git history, tests and docs
Impact, risk and dead-code answers without LLM calls
REST and MCP access with scoped tokens
Code health scores and generated docs
faq: Is Repowise free?
It is free for one developer and open source under AGPL-3.0; a commercial licence and hosted version are available for companies.

facts.license: the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

long: ai-memory, by Fabio Akita, is a long-term memory layer for AI coding agents. Coding agents each keep their own notes on one machine; ai-memory gives more than twenty harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Devin, Kiro and others) one shared memory, stored as plain markdown.

Quit Claude Code mid-task, start Codex in the same directory, and the next agent picks up a typed handoff saying where you left off, what failed and what is still open. Starting agents through ai-memory run can also carry a private local view of the previous session, and a small cross-project profile of your habits follows you into new repositories. It ships as one binary for Linux, macOS and Windows.
ai-memory.who: Developers who switch between coding agents, machines or teammates and are tired of re-explaining the project.
faq: Is ai-memory free?
Yes, it is open source under the MIT License.

long: Dodaios (formerly Personal Jarvis) is an open-source agent OS for the desktop on Windows, macOS and Linux. You talk to it by voice or chat, and a lead agent plans the work, then runs your coding CLIs side by side, your browser and your apps, taking a task from one prompt to a merged pull request.

Speech recognition and voice run offline with Whisper and Piper, and a local wiki on your disk gives agents long-term memory they can cite. It works with a local model through Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server, or with an existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription, so no API key or GPU is required. A plugin and skills marketplace is community-run.
dodaios.who: People who want a local, voice-driven assistant that runs their AI coding agents and apps without sending data to a hosted service.
features: Voice or chat control, offline speech
Runs several coding CLIs in parallel panes
Local models or existing Claude/ChatGPT subscriptions
faq: Is Dodaios free?
Yes, it is open source under Apache-2.0. You bring a local model, an API key or a Claude or ChatGPT subscription.

long: Sphinx is an open-source Git hook for agent-assisted development. When you, or your coding agent, push to a branch you protect, Git pauses and Sphinx has a reviewer model that never saw your chat read the diff and ask you what the change does when things go wrong.

Answer wrong and it explains why, then tries a new scenario; answer right and the push continues. Its pitch is that you can outsource the writing but not the understanding. It runs on few tokens using your existing coding agent, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, never shows your answers to the coding agent, never opens .env files or keys, and has a logged 'sphinx yolo' escape hatch. It reached the Hacker News front page in October 2026.
sphinx.who: Developers who ship code written by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or other agents and want to be sure they understand it before it reaches production.
features: Git pre-push quiz on protected branches
Questions generated from the actual diff
Works with Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi or plain Git
Any model: your agent, OpenRouter or OpenAI-compatible
faq: Is Sphinx free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License; you only pay for the model tokens its questions use.
How do I install it?
npm install -g sphinx-understand, then run sphinx install (Node 22.19+, macOS, Linux or WSL).

long: Reticle checks whether your AI coding agent's work is actually done. A small dev-only SDK sits inside your running web or desktop app, and your agent gets tools to look, act, observe and assert through it, reading network responses, real store state, console errors and each element's source line rather than a screenshot.

Every check ends in a verdict, yes, no or cannot tell, with the evidence and the file and line to fix. Flows you verify can be saved and replayed deterministically without an AI model (Reticle cites about 480 tokens for a four-flow suite), and 'reticle gate' fails a CI change that touches a saved flow without a new passing run. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini CLI and other MCP clients, on React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Electron and Tauri apps; the SDK is stripped from production builds.
reticle.who: Developers using coding agents on web or desktop apps who are tired of acting as the agent's QA.
features: Pass, fail or cannot-tell verdicts with file:line
Reads network, app state and console from inside the app
Saved flows replay without an AI model
CI gate for changes that touch saved flows
Hosted dashboard with run history and grouped failures
faq: Is Reticle open source?

Partly. The embeddable SDK packages are Apache-2.0; the server and CLI packages are under the Functional Source License (free for internal use, Apache-2.0 after two years), and enterprise features need a licence key.
Does it cost anything?
The hosted platform at app.reticle.sh is free to start with no credit card; paid and enterprise prices are not listed publicly.

facts.license: Apache-2.0 for the SDK packages, FSL-1.1-ALv2 for the server (source-available)

long: Manifest LLM Gateway is an open-source gateway for AI agents and apps. You connect API keys, subscriptions and local models once, and everything goes through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint; send model 'auto' and Manifest picks the model for each request, so you are not locked to one provider.

It connects to 300+ models through 35 built-in provider connections plus any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, and can reuse 18 subscription flows. It logs full request and error bodies, tracks spend with budget alerts and limits, and falls back to other models when a query fails. You can use Manifest Cloud or self-host the Docker image on Railway, Render, AWS, GCP, Fly.io and other platforms.
manifest.who: Developers and teams running agents across several model providers who want routing, fallbacks and cost tracking in one place.
features: One OpenAI-compatible endpoint, auto model routing
300+ models via 35 providers, subscriptions and local models
Spend tracking, budget alerts and limits
Fallbacks and self-healing of failed requests
faq: How much does Manifest cost?
Self-hosting is free (MIT). Manifest Cloud has a Free plan (10,000 routed requests a month) until November 1, 2026; from November 2 Manifest Cloud costs $19/month (Pro).

tiers: 10,000 routed requests a month, 7-day retention; available until Nov 1, 2026
Manifest Cloud, longer data access, unlimited agents
pricing_v.note: From November 2, 2026 Manifest Cloud is $19/month; self-hosted stays free.

long: The MCP Registry is the official, community-driven registry service for Model Context Protocol servers, run under the modelcontextprotocol project. It gives MCP clients a list of available servers, like an app store, and an API (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) that clients and sub-registries can build on.

Server authors publish their own entries, and a working group with members from Stacklok, PulseMCP and others maintains it. It launched in preview in September 2025 and its v0.1 API was frozen in October 2025 so integrators could build against a stable contract while work continues towards general availability.
mcp-registry.who: MCP client developers who need a source of servers, and MCP server authors who want to be discoverable.
features: Official list of MCP servers with a public API
Basis for client app stores and sub-registries
Run as an open community project
faq: Is the MCP Registry free?
Yes. The code is open source (Apache-2.0, transitioning from MIT) and the public registry API is free to use.

long: SD.Next, by Vladimir Mandic, is an all-in-one open-source web interface for generating and editing images and video with a wide range of diffusion models. It runs locally on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon or CPU setups, on desktop or mobile.

You can create images or video from text or images, inpaint, outpaint and refine, guide generation with LoRA, ControlNet and IP-Adapters, and caption, tag, upscale, interpolate or colorize. Models can be auto-downloaded from a reference list, SDNQ quantization and offloading help on smaller GPUs, and a built-in installer manages dependencies and updates.
sd-next.who: Artists and hobbyists who want one local interface for many image and video diffusion models on their own hardware.
features: Runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon or CPU
faq: Is SD.Next free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and runs on your own hardware.

long: GLM-5 is Z.ai's open-weights model family for coding and long-horizon agentic work, and the GitHub repository now covers GLM-5, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash. GLM-5.2 brought a stable 1M-token context and coding with selectable thinking effort, with IndexShare cutting per-token compute at long context.

GLM-5.3 keeps the 5.2 base and improves complex coding and long-horizon tasks through post-training, while GLM-5.3-Flash is a new, more efficient base with hybrid sparse and linear attention. The weights can be run yourself, and the models are also served through the Z.ai API platform and the z.ai chat app.
glm-5.who: Developers who want a strong open-weights model for coding agents and long agentic tasks, self-hosted or via API.
features: Open weights for coding and agentic tasks
Also available through the Z.ai API
faq: Is GLM-5 free?
The weights and code are published openly (the repository is Apache-2.0); using it through the Z.ai API is paid, and those prices were not verified here.

long: TripoSR is an open-source model from Tripo AI and Stability AI for fast feed-forward 3D reconstruction from a single image. Built on the Large Reconstruction Model (LRM) approach, it produces a 3D model in under half a second on an NVIDIA A100.

The code, pretrained model and demo are released under the MIT License. You run it with Python and PyTorch (about 6 GB of VRAM for one image by default), can bake a texture instead of vertex colors, and there is a local Gradio app; the technical report compares it favourably with other open-source image-to-3D models.
triposr.who: 3D artists, game developers and researchers who want quick image-to-3D meshes on their own GPU.
features: Under 0.5 s per model on an A100
faq: Is TripoSR free?
Yes. The code and pretrained model are open source under the MIT License.

long: Superagent is an open-source SDK for AI agent safety. Its Guard call detects and blocks prompt injections, malicious instructions and unsafe tool calls at runtime, and Redact strips PII, PHI and secrets from text, with TypeScript and Python clients.

It can also scan repositories for attacks aimed at AI agents, such as repo poisoning and planted instructions, and run red-team scenarios against your agent. Alongside the SDK, Superagent sells a hosted security product that is free for open-source repositories, with credit-based plans for private ones.
superagent.who: Teams building AI apps and agents that handle untrusted input or sensitive data.
faq: How much does Superagent cost?

The SDK is free and open source (MIT). The hosted service is free for open-source repositories; for private repositories there is a free tier (100 credits a month), Starter $499/month, Growth $1,499/month and Scale from $3,999/month.

tiers: SDK (MIT); hosted use free on public repositories
pricing_v.note: Annual plans include 20% more credits.

long: MobileBuildMCP, from Sentry, is an MCP server and CLI that gives coding agents the tools they need on iOS and macOS projects: building, testing and running apps with Xcode. One package covers both modes, the CLI for the terminal and the MCP server for agents such as Cursor, Claude Code and Codex.

It installs through Homebrew or npm (the Homebrew tap is getsentry/xcodebuildmcp), needs macOS 14.5+ and Xcode 16+, and ships two optional agent skills that teach the agent how to use the MCP tools or the CLI.
mobilebuildmcp.who: iOS and macOS developers who let coding agents build, test and run their Xcode projects.
features: Xcode build, test and run tools for agents
MCP server and CLI in one package
Works with Cursor, Claude Code and Codex
Optional MCP and CLI agent skills
faq: Is MobileBuildMCP free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License.
What do I need?
macOS 14.5 or later, Xcode 16 or later, and Node.js 18+ unless you install with Homebrew.

long: AIOS, from the AGI Research group, is an 'AI agent operating system' that embeds a language model into the operating system layer. Its kernel manages what agents need, such as LLM access, scheduling, context switching, memory, storage and tools, while the separate Cerebrum SDK is used to build and run agents on top.

It offers a web UI and a terminal UI, and a computer-use variant extends the kernel with a VM controller and an MCP server so agents can operate a desktop safely. It is a research project with accompanying papers rather than a commercial product.
aios.who: Researchers and developers exploring OS-level infrastructure for running many LLM agents.
features: Kernel for agent scheduling and context switching
Computer-use mode with VM controller and MCP
faq: Is AIOS free?
The code is free to download on GitHub, but the repository's LICENSE file is empty, so no open-source licence is declared.

facts.license: no licence (the LICENSE file is empty)

long: Fragments is E2B's open-source Next.js template for apps that are fully generated by AI, in the spirit of Claude Artifacts or v0. You describe what you want, a model writes the code, and it runs in a secure E2B sandbox with output streamed into the UI.

It supports Python, Next.js, Vue.js, Streamlit and Gradio stacks, can install any npm or pip package, and works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Groq, Fireworks, Together AI and Ollama models. Running it needs an E2B API key and a model provider key; a hosted demo is at fragments.e2b.dev.
fragments.who: Developers who want a starting point for their own AI app builder or code-artifact feature.
features: Python, Next.js, Vue, Streamlit and Gradio
Next.js 14, shadcn/ui and Vercel AI SDK
faq: Is Fragments free?
The template is open source under the Apache License 2.0; you pay for your E2B sandbox usage and model API keys.

long: DeepChat is an open-source, local-first AI agent desktop client that puts models, tools, skills, agent runtimes and long-running sessions in one app. It works with cloud APIs such as OpenAI, Gemini and Anthropic and with local Ollama models, and any provider in those API formats.

Sessions follow a 'keep the process' design, so context, tool calls and results stay recoverable and inspectable. It has strong MCP support, installable and exportable skills, Agent Client Protocol (ACP) integration for coding agents, and remote control of sessions from Telegram, Feishu/Lark, QQBot, Discord and WeChat.
deepchat.who: People who want one private desktop app for chatting with many models and running agents, with their data stored locally.
features: ACP agents in the model picker
Remote control from Telegram, Discord and more
faq: Is DeepChat free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0; you bring your own model API keys or local models.

long: AIO Sandbox is an all-in-one sandbox environment for AI agents that packs a browser, terminal, file system, VS Code Server, Jupyter and MCP into a single Docker container, so an agent can browse, run code and edit files in one place.

It starts with one docker run command, supports API-key authentication across its API, JupyterLab and VNC, and publishes pinned release images, including a mirror for users in mainland China. The project also provides an API, examples, a paper and an evaluation suite.
aio-sandbox.who: Developers building agents that need a combined browser, shell and code environment they can self-host.
features: Browser, shell, files, VS Code and Jupyter in one container
faq: Is AIO Sandbox free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and runs on your own Docker host.

long: Baserow is an open-source no-code platform for building databases, applications, automations and AI agents, often used as an Airtable alternative. It combines a spreadsheet-style database with app and portal publishing on your own domain, automations and dashboards.

Its AI assistant, Kuma, can create databases and workflows from natural language. Baserow is API-first, runs in the cloud or self-hosted, and cites GDPR, HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II compliance and more than 150,000 users. The core is MIT-licensed, with premium and enterprise features under separate licences.
baserow.who: Teams that want Airtable-style databases, internal apps and automations with the option to self-host.
features: Apps and portals on your own domain
Kuma AI assistant builds from prompts
faq: How much does Baserow cost?
There is a free plan. Cloud Premium is $10 per user/month billed yearly ($12 monthly), Advanced is $18 per user/month yearly ($22 monthly), and Enterprise is on request.

facts.license: the MIT License for the core (premium and enterprise features under their own licences)

tiers: 3,000 rows and 2 GB per workspace, 2,000 automation credits
250,000 rows, 100 GB, roles and audit logs
pricing_v.note: Cloud prices shown; self-hosted plans are listed separately on the same page.

long: Agents CLI, from Google, is a command-line tool plus a set of skills that turn a coding assistant into an expert at building, evaluating and deploying AI agents on Google Cloud and the Gemini platform, so you don't have to learn every CLI and service yourself.

You install it with uvx google-agents-cli setup, or add only the skills with npx skills add google/agents-cli, then ask your coding agent (Antigravity CLI, Claude Code, Codex or another) to build an agent. It covers creating, scaling, governing and optimizing agents.
agents-cli.who: Developers who build agents on Google Cloud and want their coding assistant to handle the setup and deployment.
features: Skills for building agents on Gemini and Google Cloud
Evaluate and deploy from your coding agent
Works with Antigravity CLI, Claude Code and Codex
faq: Is Agents CLI free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0; the Google Cloud services you deploy to are billed separately.

long: 21st Magic MCP lets coding agents such as Cursor, Claude Code and Windsurf search 21st.dev's catalog of React and Tailwind components, generate new UI with AI and publish your own, right from the editor. Magic MCP has now been replaced by the unified 21st MCP, installed with the 21st CLI.

The original @21st-dev/magic package is kept as a small proxy so old configurations keep working; old Magic API keys were reset, so you need a fresh key from 21st.dev/mcp. Component search and code retrieval are included in 21st plans, while AI generation uses monthly AI credits.
21st-magic-mcp.who: Front-end developers who want their coding agent to pull in or generate polished React UI components.
features: Search 21st.dev React/Tailwind components from the editor
Works with Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Codex and VS Code
faq: How much does 21st cost?
The MCP code is open source (ISC). 21st plans: Builder $6/month, Builder + AI $15/month and Team $7.50 per seat/month (billed yearly); extra AI credits are 100 for $5.

tiers: marketplace, component installs via MCP and CLI
500-2,000 monthly AI credits, PR design reviews
pricing_v.note: Extra AI credits: 100 for $5 (roll over). Searching is free with 2 installs a day.

long: SWE-bench is the benchmark that tests whether language models and coding agents can resolve real GitHub issues: given a codebase and an issue, the system must produce a patch that makes the project's tests pass. It was introduced at ICLR 2024 and is one of the most cited coding-agent benchmarks.

Variants include SWE-bench Verified, a 500-task subset that engineers confirmed solvable (with OpenAI Preparedness), and SWE-bench Multimodal for visual software tasks, whose v2 with 480 tasks became fully open source in September 2026. Evaluation runs in containers locally, on Modal, or through the sb-cli cloud tool for leaderboard submissions.
swe-bench.who: Researchers and teams who want to measure and compare coding models and agents on real-world issues.
features: Real GitHub issues with test-based grading
Cloud runs via Modal and sb-cli
faq: Is SWE-bench free?
Yes. The code and datasets are open source (MIT); you pay only for the compute and model calls your evaluation uses.

long: DevOpsGPT, from KuafuAI, is a multi-agent system that turns natural-language requirements into working software by combining large language models with DevOps tools. You describe what you need, it helps clarify the requirement, writes interface documentation and code, and works inside an existing project rather than only starting from scratch.

It then hands the result to continuous integration and can deploy the new version to your target environment. The open-source edition runs from source with Python and SQLite; an Enterprise Edition adds analysis of existing projects, stronger specialist models with private deployment and more DevOps platform integrations, and KuafuAI also offers a cloud service.
devopsgpt.who: Development teams who want an agent to go from a plain-language requirement to code, CI and deployment on their own projects.
features: Clarifies requirements and writes interface docs
Works on existing projects in any language
Hooks into CI and deployment tools
Enterprise Edition and cloud service available
faq: Is DevOpsGPT open source?

The code is public under Apache 2.0 with an added clause that forbids using it to compete directly with DevOpsGPT and KuafuAI services, so it is source-available rather than OSI open source. Enterprise and cloud pricing is not published.

facts.license: Apache 2.0 plus an extra clause that bars directly competing with DevOpsGPT and KuafuAI services

long: Apache Maka (Incubating) is an open-source agent workspace from the Apache Software Foundation incubator that keeps a complete record of everything the agent did. Every model message, tool call, permission decision and stop is stored as an append-only event log, and the UI, the next prompt and crash recovery are all built from that log.

It runs on your machine with the model you choose (a cloud API, a local model or a compatible gateway), and sessions, settings and run records stay local. A desktop app, a terminal UI and a CLI all share one runtime host, and the project publishes per-task benchmark runs against other agent harnesses on the same model and official verifier. The latest Apache release is 0.2.0 (incubating).
apache-maka.who: Developers who want a local, auditable agent harness and published, reproducible benchmark results.
features: Append-only log of every model message and tool call
Desktop app, terminal UI and CLI on one runtime
Bring your own cloud, local or gateway model
Sessions and records stay on your machine
faq: Is Apache Maka free?
