Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0; you pay only for the model you connect.

long: UltraRAG is a low-code framework for building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines on the Model Context Protocol, launched by Tsinghua University's THUNLP, Northeastern University's NEUIR, OpenBMB and partners. Core RAG parts such as retrieval and generation run as separate MCP servers, and an MCP client orchestrates them, so complex pipelines take little code.

UltraRAG 3.0 (January 2026) adds UltraRAG UI, a visual RAG development environment with a pipeline builder that keeps canvas and code in sync, an AI assistant, and a unified evaluation system. It targets both research experiments and industrial prototypes, including lightweight deep-research pipelines.
ultrarag.who: Researchers and engineers who want to assemble, debug and evaluate RAG pipelines quickly.
features: RAG components as independent MCP servers
Visual pipeline builder synced with code
faq: Is UltraRAG free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

long: OpenAgent is an open-source, self-hostable personal AI assistant that combines large language models, a knowledge base built from your own documents (RAG) and autonomous agent loops. Agents can use the browser and computer and act as a coding agent.

It ships as a single binary for Linux, macOS and Windows (x86_64 and arm64), so there is nothing else to install: the installer starts it on port 14000. You can connect any model provider, and the admin side includes usage analytics, activity monitoring, tool management and detailed logs. A live demo and playground are available.
openagent.who: People and teams who want one self-hosted assistant with their own documents, any model and agents that can browse and code.
features: Single binary for Linux, macOS and Windows
faq: Is OpenAgent free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and you host it yourself.

long: Coucou is a small open-source companion that lives in your Mac's notch, or at the top of the screen on Windows and Linux, and keeps an eye on your AI coding agent sessions. Its mascot Mochi pops out when Claude Code needs you, and you can see what each agent reads, edits and runs, approve permissions, drop in a file or chat with Claude without switching windows.

It follows Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Amp and other agents, and when you step away it moves to your iPhone or Android phone so you can approve from the Lock Screen or Dynamic Island. Version 0.4 also made it a full Mac app with hold-to-talk dictation (offline with NVIDIA Parakeet) and a call notetaker that needs no meeting bot.
coucou.who: Developers who run several coding agents and want to watch and approve them without leaving what they are doing.
features: Live view of coding agent sessions in the notch
Approve permissions from the notch or phone Lock Screen
Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and more
Call notetaker without a meeting bot
faq: Is Coucou free?
Yes. The code is open source under the MIT License; the Coucou name, Mochi and sounds remain the author's.

long: TUIOS is a terminal multiplexer and window manager written in Go that knows what your coding agents are doing. It gives you tiling panes, workspaces and a vim-like modal interface inside your existing terminal, with sessions that survive restarts.

For agents it adds one Inbox across every coding agent, with their state, approvals, fleets and agents on other machines, plus a tmux shim so tools that drive tmux, such as Claude Code agent teams, still work. It is built on the Charm stack with event-driven rendering for near-zero idle CPU, supports kitty graphics, hooks and themes, and you can try it in the browser at tuios.dev/learn.
tuios.who: Terminal users who run several coding agents and want one place to watch and approve them.
features: Tiling panes, workspaces and BSP layouts
One Inbox for every coding agent
Sessions that survive restarts and detach
tmux shim for Claude Code agent teams
Hooks, themes and a control protocol
faq: Is TUIOS free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License.

long: 5ire (pronounced 'fai-er') is a cross-platform desktop AI assistant and MCP client. It works with major model providers including OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Grok, DeepSeek and local models through Ollama.

It supports a local knowledge base and tools through Model Context Protocol servers, with one-click server installation that websites can integrate. The tools feature needs Python, Node.js and uv installed, since those run the MCP servers.
5ire.who: People who want one desktop chat app for many model providers with MCP tools and a local knowledge base.
features: Desktop assistant for Mac, Windows and Linux
Many providers plus Ollama local models
faq: Is 5ire free?
It is free to download. Its licence is a modified Apache License 2.0 with extra conditions, so check the LICENSE file before building on it.

facts.license: a modified Apache License 2.0 with extra conditions

long: Peekaboo is a macOS command-line tool and menu-bar app for screen capture, accessibility inspection and native UI automation, so an AI agent can see the screen and do the clicks. You can use it directly, let its built-in agent plan multi-step work, or expose the same tools to MCP clients such as Codex, Claude Code and Cursor.

It can return a structured map of a running app's interface with element IDs, then click, type and act on those elements. It needs macOS 15 or later and installs with Homebrew, as an npm MCP package, or as a signed Mac app that handles permission setup and shows visual feedback.
peekaboo.who: Developers who want coding or desktop agents to see and control Mac apps.
features: Screenshots of the screen or any app
Structured UI maps with element IDs
Native clicks and typing via accessibility
MCP server for Codex, Claude Code and Cursor
faq: Is Peekaboo free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License.

long: FrontierAgent, from Apodex, is an open-source agent runtime, terminal app and evaluation suite for long research and file-based tasks. Its frontier-agent terminal UI has two workflows: ReAct, where one agent researches, reads files, writes deliverables and runs commands in a task sandbox, and Agent Team, where a coordinator splits the work across parallel sub-agents and combines their reports.

The same engine runs the benchmarks Apodex uses for its own models, and the framework, tools, workflows and evaluation layer can each be reused on their own. It installs with one command on macOS and Linux with no hard Docker dependency, and works with OpenAI-compatible endpoints including Apodex's API.
frontieragent.who: Developers who want a ready-made terminal agent for long research and file tasks, single or as a team.
features: One-command install, no hard Docker dependency
faq: Is FrontierAgent free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0; you supply the model, such as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

long: AstronRPA, from iFlytek, is an open-source, enterprise-grade robotic process automation (RPA) desktop app. A visual low-code designer lets you build workflows that automate Windows desktop software and web pages, from WPS and Office to ERP systems and browsers.

It comes with 300+ ready-made actions, team sharing, scheduling and monitoring, and connects both ways with iFlytek's Astron Agent platform so automations and AI agents can call each other. Workflows can be triggered directly, on a schedule, by API or as MCP services. The client targets Windows 10/11 and the server deploys with Docker.
astronrpa.who: Businesses that want agent-ready desktop and web automation they can self-host.
features: Triggers by schedule, API or MCP
faq: Is AstronRPA free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and can be self-hosted.

long: The MCP Go SDK is the official Go software development kit for the Model Context Protocol, maintained by the MCP project in collaboration with Google. It provides the main APIs for building MCP clients and servers, transport packages, and OAuth helpers.

The SDK aims to implement the full MCP specification, and its documentation maps each part of the spec to its packages, with a table of which SDK versions support which protocol versions. Features deprecated in the 2026-07-28 protocol version, such as roots, sampling and logging, stay supported for compatibility.
mcp-go-sdk.who: Go developers building MCP servers or clients for AI agents.
features: Version table against the MCP spec
faq: Is the MCP Go SDK free?
Yes. It is open source (Apache-2.0, transitioning from MIT).

long: Sparrow, from Katana ML, is an API-first platform for document intelligence: it turns invoices, receipts, bank statements, forms and tables into clean, validated JSON using machine learning, LLMs and vision LLMs, all running on your own infrastructure.

Besides extraction it handles instruction processing such as validation and decisions, and has an agent framework for multi-step workflows monitored through Prefect. Pipelines mix vision and text models, and the same API works on MLX on Apple Silicon, vLLM on NVIDIA, Ollama, Hugging Face or Mistral OCR. A web UI offers drag-and-drop uploads and JSON schema queries.
sparrow.who: Teams that need structured data from business documents without sending them to a third party.
features: Document to validated JSON via REST
Vision LLM and text LLM pipelines
Runs on MLX, vLLM, Ollama or Hugging Face
faq: Is Sparrow free?
The code is open source under the GNU GPL v3.0 and you can self-host it; commercial licensing terms were not checked here.

long: Kiln is a workbench for the whole AI development loop: evals, optimization, prompts, RAG, fine-tuning, synthetic data, agents and tools in one app. Desktop apps for Mac, Windows and Linux let product managers, subject experts and QA contribute alongside engineers, and projects sync to Git automatically.

Its eval builder auto-generates a judge and synthetic eval set, Auto-Optimize searches prompts, models, tools and parameters, and the Kiln Assistant proposes and runs experiments. You can build a RAG by dragging in PDFs, images, video or audio, compose sub-agent hierarchies, and fine-tune 60+ models on Fireworks, Together or Vertex without code.
kiln.who: Teams building AI products who want evals, optimization and fine-tuning in one collaborative tool.
faq: Is Kiln free?
Yes. The desktop app is free under the Kiln AI Desktop EULA, and the Python libraries are open source under the MIT License.

facts.license: MIT for the Python libraries; the desktop app is free under the Kiln AI Desktop EULA

long: MCPorter is a TypeScript runtime and command-line tool for discovering and calling Model Context Protocol servers. It lets developers and coding agents use the same MCP tools from a terminal, a script, or a standalone CLI that MCPorter generates.

You can list a server's tools as TypeScript-style signatures and call them directly, with JSON output when another program needs it. It reads project and user config and imports MCP servers already set up in Cursor, Claude Code and Desktop, Codex, Windsurf, OpenCode and VS Code. It installs with npx, npm or Homebrew.
mcporter.who: Developers and agents that want to call MCP tools from scripts and the command line.
features: Call any MCP server from the terminal
Imports configs from Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and more
faq: Is MCPorter free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License.

long: Sphere SDK is a modular TypeScript SDK from Unicity for giving autonomous agents an identity and a wallet on the Unicity network, so they can find, negotiate with and settle payments with other agents peer to peer.

It covers BIP39/BIP32 wallet keys with optional seed encryption, certified token transfers and payment requests with encrypted memos, a signed intent bulletin board with semantic search, and Nostr-based direct and group messaging. It runs in the browser or in Node.js 22+, and a Connect protocol lets dApps talk to a hosted wallet.
sphere-sdk.who: Developers building agents that need to hold funds and pay or get paid by other agents.
features: Certified token transfers and payment requests
faq: Is Sphere SDK free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License and installs from npm as @unicitylabs/sphere-sdk.

long: SkillHub, from iFlytek, is a self-hosted, open-source registry for agent skills. Teams publish skill packages into namespaces, version them, and let colleagues find them through search or install them with a CLI, all behind their own firewall.

It adds governance for companies, with role-based access control and audit logs, and deploys on-premise with Docker or Kubernetes. A REST API (with Python examples) handles search, download and publishing, and there is a curated starter collection of community skills.
skillhub.who: Organizations that want a private, governed place to share agent skills internally.
faq: Is SkillHub free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and you host it yourself.

long: EvoScientist is an open-source AI scientist system that explores research ideas, runs experiments and writes up results, while improving itself through growing skills and memory. It works 'human on the loop': the researcher steers while a team of six sub-agents handles planning, research, coding, debugging, analysis and writing.

Memory is distilled every turn into a self-linking knowledge graph, and AutoSkills turns recurring patterns into reusable skills you approve. It switches between Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, MiniMax and NVIDIA models, runs from a CLI, a desktop web UI or chat apps such as Telegram and Slack, can schedule recurring research, and plugs in MCP servers and skills.
evoscientist.who: Researchers who want an autonomous research assistant that plans, codes, analyzes and writes.
features: CLI, web UI and chat-app access
faq: Is EvoScientist free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0; you pay for the model provider you connect.

long: Zep is a managed memory and context platform for AI agents. It builds a temporal knowledge graph from conversations, business data and documents, so agents can recall relevant facts and how they changed over time. It is powered by Zep's open-source Graphiti framework.

Official SDKs cover Python, TypeScript and Go, and integration packages exist for frameworks such as Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, LiveKit, Pydantic AI, Mastra and the Vercel AI SDK. A bulk ingestion pipeline loads Slack, documents, email and CSV data, and plugins bring Zep memory to Claude Code, Codex and Cursor. The older self-hosted Community Edition is deprecated.
zep.who: Teams building agents that need long-term, up-to-date memory about users and business data.
features: Bulk ingestion from Slack, docs and email
faq: Is Zep open source?
Zep Cloud is a managed service with a free plan and paid tiers. The getzep/zep repository holds Apache-2.0 examples and integrations, and the graph engine underneath, Graphiti, is open source.

facts.license: Apache 2.0 for the examples and integrations repo; Zep Cloud itself is a managed service

long: ACE-Step is an open-source foundation model for music generation. It combines diffusion-based generation with a deep-compression autoencoder and a lightweight linear transformer to get both speed and long-range musical structure.

The team reports it can create up to four minutes of music in about 20 seconds on an A100 GPU, about 15 times faster than LLM-based baselines, with good lyric alignment. It also supports voice cloning, lyric editing, remixing and track generation such as lyrics to vocals or singing to accompaniment. Weights are on Hugging Face and ModelScope, with a demo Space and a training guide.
ace-step.who: Musicians and developers who want a fast, open model for generating and editing full songs.
features: Full songs up to four minutes
Fast generation on a single GPU
faq: Is ACE-Step free?
Yes. The code and model are released under the Apache License 2.0.

long: MonkeyCode, from Chaitin, is an open-source AI development platform for professional engineering teams. It combines development environment management, AI model management, AI task management and project requirement management, so you can hand it a requirement and it carries the work through development and validation.

Teams can deploy it inside their own network and manage AI coding workflows centrally, or use the online version with managed cloud environments, built-in models and iOS and Android apps. Every task runs in a real server-side environment with build, test and preview, and it supports models such as GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Qwen and DeepSeek.
monkeycode.who: Engineering teams that want a self-hostable AI coding platform with central control.
faq: Is MonkeyCode free?
The code is open source under the GNU AGPL v3.0 and you can self-host it; the online version is free to start. Paid plan pricing was not verified.

long: Thunderbolt is an open-source, cross-platform AI client from the Thunderbird team, built around choosing your own models and keeping your own data. It runs on the web, iOS, Android, Mac, Linux and Windows, and works with frontier, local and on-prem models.

It is still early and under active development, aimed first at enterprises that want to deploy it on-prem, with enterprise support available. You can self-host the backend with Docker Compose, add keys for any OpenAI-compatible provider, or point it at Ollama or llama.cpp for free local inference.
thunderbolt.who: Organizations and individuals who want a private AI client they can host and point at any model.
faq: Is Thunderbolt free?
Yes. It is open source under the Mozilla Public License 2.0; enterprise support pricing is not published.

long: DeepAnalyze, from Renmin University of China and Tsinghua University, is an agentic large language model built for autonomous data science. It can carry out a whole data science pipeline on its own: data preparation, analysis, modeling, visualization and report writing.

It also does open-ended research across structured data (databases, CSV, Excel), semi-structured data (JSON, XML, YAML) and plain text, and produces analyst-grade reports. The 8B model, the code and the 500K-example training dataset are all public, with a paper on arXiv.
deepanalyze.who: Analysts and researchers who want an open model that analyzes data and writes the report.
features: Works on databases, spreadsheets and JSON
faq: Is DeepAnalyze free?
Yes. The code is open source under the MIT License and the model and data are published on Hugging Face.

long: Latitude is an open-source observability platform for AI agents that finds where agents fail and helps get them fixed. One line of telemetry captures multi-turn sessions, tool calls and full execution paths, with OpenTelemetry ingest.

Failing traces are grouped into tracked signals with size and trend. Latitude can then send your coding agent, such as Claude Code or Cursor, the context and sample traces to write a fix and open a pull request, and replays fixes against the real failing traces so regressions don't return. Everything in the UI is also available through its MCP server.
latitude.who: Teams running agents in production who want to find, fix and verify failures quickly.
features: Dispatch coding agents to fix issues
faq: Is Latitude free?
The code is open source under the MIT License and can be self-hosted; a hosted cloud is also offered, but its pricing was not verified here.

long: SwarmUI (formerly StableSwarmUI) is a modular web interface for running AI image, video and some audio models on your own hardware. It supports image models such as Stable Diffusion and Flux, video models such as Wan and LTX-2, and audio models such as ACE-Step.

Beginners can use the simple Generate tab, while advanced users can open the full ComfyUI workflow graph underneath. It adds convenience tools like an image editor, automatic workflow generation and a grid generator, and is in near-release beta (v0.9.8).
swarmui.who: Hobbyists and pros who want one local interface for image and video models, from simple to node-based.
features: Image, video and audio model support
faq: Is SwarmUI free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License and runs on your own GPU.

long: Agency Swarm is a Python framework for building multi-agent applications on top of the OpenAI Agents SDK. It models automation like a real organization: you define agents with roles such as CEO, virtual assistant or developer, each with its own instructions and tools.

Agents talk to each other through a dedicated send_message tool along communication flows you define, tools are type-safe Pydantic models, and you keep full control of every prompt. It was started by Arsenii Shatokhin (VRSEN), and version 1.x is a rewrite on the Agents SDK with a migration guide from 0.x.
agency-swarm.who: Developers who want to build teams of role-based agents on the OpenAI Agents SDK.
features: Built on the OpenAI Agents SDK
faq: Is Agency Swarm free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License; you pay for the models you call.

long: AutoDev, by Phodal, is a multi-agent development platform built on Kotlin Multiplatform. Version 3.0, called AutoDev Xiuper (alpha), covers document research, coding, code review, data queries, artifact generation and web interaction workflows from one shared agent engine.

It runs as an IntelliJ IDEA plugin, a VS Code extension, a CLI (npm @xiuper/cli), a web app, desktop and Android builds and a remote coding-agent server, with MCP integration and AGENTS.md support. The earlier AutoDev 2.0 remains available as the stable IntelliJ plugin.
autodev.who: Developers who want one agent platform across their IDE, terminal, desktop and phone.
features: IntelliJ, VS Code, CLI and web
faq: Is AutoDev free?
Yes. It is open source under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.

long: Kungfu is a workspace that keeps one piece of work moving across different coding agents, so you don't have to copy context and re-explain decisions every time you switch. You can use a strong agent when it matters and a cheaper one when it doesn't, across Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Amp or your own execution surface.

It tracks each piece of work through attempts, so a task can survive a disconnect or crash and recover. It is in alpha, installs on macOS or Linux with a per-user script that needs no sudo, and includes a mock agent to test recovery without provider credentials.
kungfu.who: Developers who switch between coding agents and want the task and its context to carry over.
features: Same task across Codex, Claude, OpenCode and Amp
faq: Is Kungfu free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

long: Observal is a self-hosted registry and system of record for a team's coding agent resources: skills, agent files and MCP servers. It gives an organization one place to discover what colleagues have already built, instead of everyone writing their own version in scattered repos.

It also has a built-in insight engine that shows how those resources are actually used, closing the feedback loop for the people who maintain them. You set the scope, share resources with peers, and coding agents use it through observal-cli.
observal.who: Engineering orgs that want to share and measure internal skills, MCP servers and agents.
features: Registry for skills, agents and MCP servers
faq: Is Observal free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and you host it yourself.

long: Kiro Crew is an open-source, persistent development workspace from the Kiro team that runs locally or on your own remote hardware. It keeps working beyond a single session and learns and improves as it goes.

Multi-step tasks can run unattended, recurring jobs run on a schedule, and heartbeats watch systems until something needs attention. You can work with it from a desktop app, a web dashboard or a CLI, or through Slack and Discord, and Kiro Crew Apps bundle a purpose-built interface with agents, skills, schedules and integrations. The default agent runs on kiro-cli, which you install and sign in to separately.
kiro-crew.who: Developers who want a self-hosted agent workspace for long-running and recurring coding work.
features: Desktop app, web dashboard and CLI
faq: Is Kiro Crew free?
The workspace is open source under the Apache License 2.0; its default agent uses kiro-cli, which needs a Kiro sign-in and follows Kiro's own plans.

long: MS-Agent, from Alibaba's ModelScope team, is a modular open-source agent framework built for complex, long-running tasks. You combine models, tools, skills and sub-agents inside a customizable harness that handles planning, context, permissions and execution.

One shared Python SDK drives a CLI, a TUI and a WebUI, so the same agent logic works in a terminal, a browser workspace or a business app. Recent releases added context compression with token monitoring, multimodal input, knowledge search over local code and docs, an Agent Hub for syncing agent workspaces with ModelScope, and Agentic Insight v2, a deep research system.
ms-agent.who: Python developers building long-running assistants, deep research or code generation agents.
features: Harness for planning, context and permissions
CLI, TUI and WebUI from one SDK
Deep research and code generation projects
faq: Is MS-Agent free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0; you pay only for the models you call.

long: CodeGraphContext (CGC) turns a code repository into a queryable graph for AI agents. It parses code with Tree-sitter (and optional SCIP indexers) into a graph database of files, symbols, calls, inheritance and imports.

You can use it as a standalone CLI for code analysis, or connect it to an AI IDE as an MCP server so the assistant can answer questions like how a call chain connects across files. Typical uses are tracing call chains, mapping class hierarchies and module boundaries, and finding dead code, hotspots and unexpected dependencies. It installs with pip.
codegraphcontext.who: Developers who want their coding assistant to understand how a large codebase fits together.
features: Code graph of files, symbols and calls
faq: Is CodeGraphContext free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License.

long: Basic Memory gives AI assistants persistent memory stored as plain Markdown files that both you and the AI can read, write and search. It works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT and any client that speaks MCP, so you can pick up a project where you left off instead of re-explaining it.

Notes build a knowledge graph through observations and wikilinks, with semantic search and optional reranking. The local version keeps everything on your disk and works air-gapped; an optional cloud workspace adds hosting, backups and cross-device sync on web, desktop and mobile.
basic-memory.who: People who want their AI assistants to remember projects across sessions, with notes they own.
faq: How much does Basic Memory cost?

The local version is free and open source under the GNU AGPL v3.0. Cloud sync starts at $15 per seat per month, and a Business plan with SSO, audit logs and admin controls is $30 per seat per month, both with a 7-day trial (checked Oct 24, 2026).

long: Container Use, from Dagger, gives each coding agent its own containerized development environment, so several agents can work in parallel without stepping on each other. Every agent gets a fresh container on its own git branch, and failed experiments can be thrown away instantly.

It is an open-source MCP server that runs as a CLI with Claude Code, Cursor, Goose and other MCP-compatible agents. You can see the full command history and logs of what an agent did, drop into its terminal to take over, and review its work with a normal git checkout. It is in early development.
container-use.who: Developers who run several coding agents at once and want them isolated and reviewable.
faq: Is Container Use free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

long: APM (Agent Package Manager) is Microsoft's open-source dependency manager for AI agent configuration, like package.json but for agents. You declare a project's skills, prompts, instructions, agents, hooks, plugins and MCP servers once in an apm.yml file.

Running apm install then sets up the same configuration for everyone who clones the repo, across GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini, Windsurf, Kiro and others, with transitive dependencies and a lockfile for reproducible installs. Packages can come from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, and organizations can set policies on what is allowed.
apm-agent-package-manager.who: Teams that want every developer's coding agents configured the same way from one manifest.
features: One manifest for skills, prompts and MCP servers
Install from GitHub, GitLab and more
faq: Is APM free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License.

long: Playwriter lets AI agents control your own running Chrome browser through a Chrome extension, a CLI or an MCP server. Because it connects to the browser you already use, your logins, extensions and cookies are already there.

Agents run Playwright code snippets in stateful sandbox sessions with the full Playwright API, can take accessibility snapshots of pages, and can be grouped into tab groups per session. A skill teaches agents how to use it, and it can also start a separate Chrome for Testing or Chromium with the extension bundled.
playwriter.who: Developers who want an agent to automate tasks in their real, logged-in browser.
faq: Is Playwriter free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License, and the extension is on the Chrome Web Store.

long: Codeg is a multi-agent coding workspace that runs many AI coding agents in one place and lets them work together. Nineteen agents are built in, and any agent that speaks ACP can join, all shown as the same structured conversation with tool cards, live diffs and interactive replies.

It can import, search and resume the session history agents keep on disk and hand it to a different agent, delegate across agents with an @ mention, and queue to-dos that run unattended in their own worktrees. It runs as a desktop app, a self-hosted server or Docker, with iPhone, iPad and Android access and Telegram, Lark or WeChat bots.
codeg.who: Developers who use several coding agents and want them in one workspace that shares history.
features: Nineteen built-in agents plus any ACP agent
faq: Is Codeg free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

long: LeanCTX is a context gateway that sits between AI tools and the information they read. It selects task-relevant context with search, structural views, compression and reuse, applies configured path permissions, content filters and context budgets, and records the context operations it can observe.

The open-source LeanCTX Engine runs locally through a CLI, an MCP server, hooks and supported proxy paths, and an SDK embeds its capabilities in your own app. Your application, agent loop and model stay your own; organization-wide controls are offered as a separate licensed Enterprise option.
leanctx.who: Developers and teams who want to control and trim what context their AI tools see.
faq: Is LeanCTX free?
The LeanCTX Engine is open source under the Apache License 2.0. Enterprise pricing is not published.

long: Hyperresearch is a deep research harness that turns Claude Code or OpenAI Codex into a deep research agent. A multi-step pipeline takes one prompt, gathers and verifies sources, and writes a cited report, while saving the research into a persistent, searchable wiki that builds on itself.

It checks that each cited source actually supports its sentence before a report ships, groups reprints of the same story so they count as one source, and has critic agents review drafts. A scholar search covers OpenAlex, Crossref, CORE, DOAB, ClinicalTrials.gov, SEC EDGAR and FRED. It installs with pip, and a hosted version with an API and MCP runs the same pipeline without a local install.
hyperresearch.who: Researchers and analysts who want long, well-cited research reports from their coding agent.
features: Deep research pipeline for Claude Code and Codex
faq: Is Hyperresearch free?
The harness is open source under the MIT License. Pricing for the hosted version was not verified.

long: SimpleMem is a research-backed memory library that gives LLM agents efficient long-term memory. It stores, compresses and retrieves memories, and since version 2.0 (Omni-SimpleMem) it handles images, audio and video as well as text. The work was accepted at ICML 2026.

One Python package picks the text or multimodal backend automatically, and the text memory is also available as an MCP server for clients such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, LM Studio and Cherry Studio. EvolveMem (v3.0) adds retrieval that tunes itself through an automated research loop, and scripts are included to reproduce the paper results.
simplemem.who: Agent builders and researchers who need compact lifelong memory, including multimodal memory.
faq: Is SimpleMem free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License; you supply the model API it calls.

long: Atmosphere is a real-time engine for AI agents on the JVM. One @Agent class can run on Spring AI, LangChain4j, Anthropic or other backends through a single runtime interface with twelve adapters, and tokens stream to clients over WebSocket, SSE, long-polling or gRPC, with optional WebTransport over HTTP/3.

Agents come with memory, planning, a virtual filesystem and sub-agent delegation by default. It adds governance such as policy checks, human approvals, cost ceilings, PII rewriting and kill switches, durable sessions that resume long runs, and an optional session tape for replay. The same agent can be exposed over MCP, A2A and AG-UI and to Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp and Messenger, inside Spring Boot, Quarkus or any servlet container.
atmosphere.who: Java teams that need production-grade, streaming AI agents inside their existing JVM stack.
features: One agent class across many AI backends
Streaming over WebSocket, SSE and gRPC
faq: Is Atmosphere free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

long: Easel, from Zhejiang University's REAL lab, is an open-source content workspace for social media creators. It connects an OpenClaw agent with account profiles, content skills and real media tools, so the agent actually produces the content instead of only giving advice.

It works in five steps: discover trends and opportunities that suit the account, plan topics, titles, scripts and a calendar, create posts, cards, audio and video, publish to the platforms, and analyze performance to feed back into the account profile. It currently supports Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Zhihu, Bilibili, WeChat Channels and WeChat Official Accounts, through a web front end or a CLI.
easel.who: Creators and marketers running accounts on Chinese social media platforms.
faq: Is Easel free?
Yes. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0; you supply the model and media tool access it uses.

long: LazyCodex is an agent harness for complex codebases that runs inside OpenAI Codex. It adds project memory, planning, execution and verified completion on top of Codex, so long tasks are planned, carried out and checked rather than stopped halfway.
It brings the oh-my-openagent (OmO) harness to Codex and installs with a single npx lazycodex-ai install command, with no global npm install needed, plus a fully automatic setup mode.
lazycodex.who: Codex users who want more structured planning and verification on large codebases.
faq: Is LazyCodex free?
Yes. It is open source under the MIT License; you need your own Codex access.

long: Knowhere is a document parsing and retrieval system that turns messy files into persistent, navigable memory for AI agents and RAG, especially for local and offline document collections. One pipeline handles parsing, hierarchy reconstruction, multimodal structuring and graph building, and every result stays linked to its document, section and source.

Version 2.0 has two tracks: a text track that keeps precise extracted structure, and a vision track that lets vision models read complex PDFs and slide decks as pages. It handles very long PDFs and technical atlases, and offers agent-native retrieval tools. You can self-host the full stack or use the managed Knowhere Cloud API.
knowhere.who: Teams building agents or RAG over large, messy document collections.
faq: Is Knowhere free?
The code is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and can be self-hosted. Knowhere Cloud gives $5 in free credits on sign-up; paid usage pricing was not verified.

long: The Google Antigravity SDK is a Python library for building AI agents powered by Antigravity and Gemini. It provides a stateful infrastructure layer that runs the agent loop for you, so you focus on what your agent does rather than how it runs.

It installs from PyPI as google-antigravity, which includes the compiled runtime binary the SDK needs (cloning the repo alone is not enough). It works with a Gemini API key or with Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), and the repo includes getting-started examples.
antigravity-sdk.who: Python developers building agents on Gemini and Google's Antigravity runtime.
features: Gemini API or Vertex AI auth
faq: Is the Antigravity SDK free?
The SDK is open source under the Apache License 2.0; Gemini model usage is billed by Google under its own pricing.

tiers: unlimited local browser processing up to 16 MP (8,192 px per side), no watermark, no card
pricing_v.note: Cloud Standard HD uses 1–4 credits per image and AI Retouch uses 4–7 credits per image (batch up to 10 images).

facts.status: Active web app (local browser processing + optional cloud HD/Retouch credits)

long: EnhanceWizard is a browser-based photo enhancer and upscaler built around two processing paths: a free local browser mode and optional paid cloud models. In the free tier, images up to 16 MP (8,192 pixels per side) run directly inside your browser on your own device, so photos are not uploaded to a server, require no account or credit card, and export without watermarks or daily count limits.

Beyond general 2x and 4x upscaling, EnhanceWizard includes task-specific workflows for unblurring, noise reduction, old photo restoration, black-and-white photo colorization, portrait enhancement, real estate and e-commerce product shots, anime and pixel art, plus print utilities such as a 300 DPI converter and image splitter. When a photo needs heavier reconstruction or batch processing up to 10 images at once, users can spend cloud credits on Standard HD (1–4 credits per image) or AI Retouch (4–7 credits per image).
enhancewizard.who: Photographers, e-commerce sellers, designers and everyday users who want a watermark-free browser upscaler that keeps routine 2x/4x enhancements local on their device, with pay-as-you-go cloud credits available for harder restorations and batch runs. Skip it if you need a developer REST API or native desktop RAW cataloging software.
features: Local browser enhancement and 2x/4x upscaling up to 16 MP (8,192 px per side) with no sign-up, daily cap or watermark.
Cloud Standard HD (1–4 credits) and AI Retouch (4–7 credits) modes for heavier detail recovery and batch runs up to 10 images.

long: Orbi is an open-source software factory for GitHub repositories that turns labelled GitHub Issues into reviewed, merged pull requests and tagged releases. When a maintainer adds the ai-ready label to an Issue, Orbi spins up an isolated git worktree, runs a coding agent (such as Claude Code or Codex) to implement the change and open a pull request, and then launches a separate, independent AI review session with fresh context to verify every acceptance criterion and repair failing checks.

Rather than letting the implementation agent grade its own work, Orbi enforces a six-point merge gate—requiring an explicit reviewer verdict, satisfied acceptance criteria, green CI checks, a clean branch and an exact commit-SHA match between the reviewed revision and the merge target.
